But שָׁכְרוּ וְלֹא־יַיִן (Yeshayahu 29:9) is that they are drunk and not from wine, and וּשְׁכֻרַת וְלֹא מִיָּיִן (Yeshayahu 51:21) is one drunk with troubles and not with wine. Where the verb takes an object it is to make drunk: וְהִשְׁכַּרְתִּים לְמַעַן יַעֲלֹזוּ (Yirmiyahu 51:39), I will make them drunk that they may exult, and אַשְׁכִּיר חִצַּי מִדָּם (Devarim 32:42), I will make My arrows drunk with blood.

Being drunk with wine, he says, is to drink what being sated is to food; but a man may drink until he neither feels nor understands. וְהוּא שִׁכֹּר עַד־מְאֹד (Shmuel I 25:36), he was very drunk, and וַיַּחְשְׁבֶהָ עֵלִי לְשִׁכֹּרָה (Shmuel I 1:13), Eli took her for a drunken woman.

Wine is called שֵׁכָר because it makes drunk, שֵׁכָר יִרְדֹּפוּ (Yeshayahu 5:11), they run after strong drink; and a drink made from fruit that makes drunk carries the name as well. In יַיִן וְשֵׁכָר אַל־תֵּשְׁתְּ (Vayikra 10:9), drink no wine or strong drink, the word takes in everything that intoxicates, even what is not wine, and he brings Chazal in Nazir: one who ate pressed figs of Keilah, or drank milk or honey, and entered the Mikdash is liable.

בַּקֹּדֶשׁ הַסֵּךְ נֶסֶךְ שֵׁכָר (Bamidbar 28:7), in the holy place pour a libation of strong drink: a libation of wine that makes drunk, and it is חי, undiluted. He brings the Sifri on Pinchas, that the quarter of a hin is poured undiluted and not mixed; and the Midrash on מִיַּיִן וְשֵׁכָר יַזִּיר, where Rabbi Elazar HaKappar reads יַיִן as the mixed wine and שֵׁכָר as the undiluted, and the same proof settles it that way round and not the reverse.

אֶשְׁכָּר יַקְרִיבוּ (Tehillim 72:10), they shall bring a gift, and הֵשִׁיבוּ אֶשְׁכָּרֵךְ (Yechezkel 27:15), they brought back your gift. He glosses it a מנחה, an offering, and says the word may have four root letters.

מור.sense: The spice מֹר, myrrh, of the anointing oil and of the oil of myrrh.

more.t: מָר־דְּרוֹר (Shemos 30:23), pure myrrh, and בְּשֶׁמֶן הַמֹּר (Esther 2:12), with oil of myrrh. The Ibn Ezra reports that some explained it as musk, and holds against them that if it were musk the pasuk could not say אָרִיתִי מוֹרִי (Shir HaShirim 5:1), I have gathered my myrrh, since musk is no plant that one gathers; he takes it for a spice of the kinds that are gathered. Rabbeinu Hai explains it as the resin of a sweet-smelling tree, which he gives by its Arabic name, and on that explanation too the word may be gathered.

From Midrash Chazis, on צְרוֹר הַמּוֹר, the bundle of myrrh: as myrrh is the chief of all the spices, so Avraham Avinu is the chief of all the tzaddikim; as whoever gathers myrrh has his hands made bitter, so Avraham Avinu made himself bitter; and as myrrh gives off its scent only in fire, so Avraham Avinu made his good deeds known only in the fiery furnace.

שֹבר.sense: To consider a thing and weigh it; and a second sense, to hope, with שֵׂבֶר for hope.

more.t: וָאֱהִי שֹׂבֵר בְּחוֹמֹת יְרוּשָׁלַם (Nechemiah 2:13), and I was considering the walls of Yerushalayim: the sense is one who thinks the matter over, from the סברא, the reasoning, of Chazal's language.

In the second sense it is to hope: לֹא־יְשַׂבְּרוּ יוֹרְדֵי־בוֹר אֶל־אֲמִתֶּךָ (Yeshayahu 38:19), those who go down to the pit do not hope for Your truth; עֵינֵי כֹל אֵלֶיךָ יְשַׂבֵּרוּ (Tehillim 145:15), the eyes of all hope to You; and הֲלָהֵן תְּשַׂבֵּרְנָה (Rus 1:13), would you wait for them. The noun is שִׂבְרוֹ, his hope, at Tehillim 146:5.

שׁבר.sense: To break, and from it שֵׁבֶר; מִשְׁבָּר, a breaker of the sea, and מַשְׁבֵּר, the womb; a dream's breaking open, which is its meaning; and שֶׁבֶר, grain.

more.t: וְלֹא שָׁבַר אֶת־הַחֲמוֹר (Melachim I 13:28), it did not break the donkey, and וּשְׁבָרָהּ כְּשֵׁבֶר נֵבֶל יוֹצְרִים (Yeshayahu 30:14), he shall break it as a potter's jar is broken; וְעֶצֶם לֹא תִשְׁבְּרוּ־בוֹ (Shemos 12:46), you shall not break a bone in it. The nouns are שֵׁבֶר, a breaking, as וּמִשֵּׁבֶר רוּחַ תְּיֵלִילוּ (Yeshayahu 65:14), you shall howl for breaking of spirit, and שִׁבְרוֹן, as הֵאָנַח בְּשִׁבְרוֹן מָתְנַיִם (Yechezkel 21:11), groan with breaking of loins.

אַחַת מֵהֵנָּה לֹא נִשְׁבָּרָה (Tehillim 34:21), not one of them is broken, is stressed on the earlier syllable, and is the verb in the past; רוּחַ נִשְׁבָּרָה (Tehillim 51:19), a broken spirit, is stressed on the last, and stands as a description.

כָּל־מִשְׁבָּרֶיךָ וְגַלֶּיךָ עָלַי עָבָרוּ (Yonah 2:4), all Your breakers and Your waves passed over me, is the breaking of the sea's waves in the storm; and from it, carried over, מִשְׁבְּרֵי־מָוֶת (Shmuel II 22:5), the breakers of death. עַד־הַשְּׁבָרִים (Yehoshua 7:5) is a place called by the name because they were broken there.

The womb is called מַשְׁבֵּר for the breaking of the woman in labour and her pangs: כִּי בָאוּ בָנִים עַד־מַשְׁבֵּר (Yeshayahu 37:3), the children have come to the birthstool, and כִּי־עֵת לֹא־יַעֲמֹד בְּמִשְׁבַּר בָּנִים (Hoshea 13:13). From the same he reads הַאֲנִי אַשְׁבִּיר וְלֹא אוֹלִיד (Yeshayahu 66:9), shall I bring to the birth and not deliver, as bringing the woman to that hour. And וָאֶשְׁבֹּר עָלָיו חֻקִּי he takes as cutting a covenant and decreeing a statute upon it that shall not be passed, breaking being said of a covenant here as cutting is said of one.

more.h: The breaking open of a dream
more.t: אֶת־מִסְפַּר הַחֲלוֹם וְאֶת־שִׁבְרוֹ (Shoftim 7:15), the telling of the dream and its breaking, he glosses as its interpretation: until it is interpreted the dream is like a thing sealed up, and the interpretation breaks it open and lays it bare.

more.h: Grain, and the buying of it
more.t: כִּי יֶשׁ־שֶׁבֶר בְּמִצְרָיִם (Bereishis 42:1), there is grain in Mitzrayim, and וַיִּשְׂאוּ אֶת־שִׁבְרָם (Bereishis 42:26), they loaded their grain: grain and any food. It may be called so, he suggests, because it breaks hunger, as יִשְׁבְּרוּ פְרָאִים צְמָאָם (Tehillim 104:11), the wild donkeys break their thirst. The buyer of it is himself called שׁוֹבֵר, one who breaks: לְכוּ שִׁבְרוּ וֶאֱכֹלוּ (Yeshayahu 55:1), go, buy and eat. So is the seller, וַיִּשְׁבֹּר לְמִצְרַיִם (Bereishis 41:56), he sold to Mitzrayim; and where the verb takes an object, הוּא הַמַּשְׁבִּיר לְכָל־עַם הָאָרֶץ (Bereishis 42:6), he it was who sold to all the people of the land.

עלם.sense: To be hidden, and to hide; עֶלֶם and עַלְמָה, a youth and a young woman; and עוֹלָם, a long or an everlasting time.

more.t: וְנֶעְלַם דָּבָר (Vayikra 4:13), the matter is hidden, and וְנֶעֶלְמָה מֵעֵינֵי כָל־חָי (Iyov 28:21), hidden from the eyes of all living. תְּהִי נַעֲלָמָה (Nachum 3:11) he glosses as though you had never been at all. To hide oneself is וְהִתְעַלַּמְתָּ מֵהֶם (Devarim 22:1), and you hide yourself from them, and to hide is אַל־תַּעְלֵם אָזְנְךָ (Eichah 3:56), do not hide Your ear.

וְאַעְלִים עֵינַי בּוֹ (Shmuel I 12:3), and I hid my eyes at him, he reads three ways: that a man took a ransom and hid his eyes from the judgment, so as not to judge as he should; or that he hid his eyes at the giver of the ransom, covering him and not uncovering his crime; and his father read it that he was ashamed to speak before the man from whom he took it, and hid his eyes from looking at him.

עֲלֻמֵנוּ לִמְאוֹר פָּנֶיךָ (Tehillim 90:8) he glosses as our errors, since a man's errors are hidden from him, and תַּעֲלֻמוֹת לֵב (Tehillim 44:22) are the heart's hidden things. So too עַל־עֲלָמוֹת שִׁיר (Tehillim 46:1), which he reads as the hidden part of the song and its secrets. Some would read וְהוּא יְנַהֲגֵנוּ עַל־מוּת (Tehillim 48:15) from hiding as well; but the Masoretic note has it as two words, עַל מוּת, and so the accurate sefarim, and then it means עַד מָוֶת, until death: He will lead us until our dying.

more.h: Whether a young woman is a virgin
more.t: וְהָיָה הָעַלְמָה הַיֹּצֵאת לִשְׁאֹב (Bereishis 24:43) is the young woman, and he holds the word covers the virgin and the one who has known a man alike, as נערה does. הִנֵּה הָעַלְמָה הָרָה (Yeshayahu 7:14) he takes of one who had known a man, the wife of the navi or the wife of his brother, and says on clear proofs that Immanuel is not Chizkiyahu. וְדֶרֶךְ גֶּבֶר בְּעַלְמָה (Mishlei 30:19) cannot be a virgin either: the things wondered at there leave no trace, the eagle's way in the sky and the snake's upon the rock, and so a man's way with an almah, where the act is not to be told; with a virgin it would be plain beyond doubt. His father brought further proofs in Sefer HaBris: were almah a virgin, there would be no עֶלֶם, a young man, formed from it, just as there is no masculine formed from בתולה, a virgin.

more.h: The youth, and why Shaul asked
more.t: בֶּן־מִי־זֶה הָעָלֶם (Shmuel I 17:56) is the youth. Shaul was not asking who he was, having already sent for him to play before him; but seeing his might as he came back from striking the Pelishti, he asked whether he was the son of a mighty man. So at בֶּן־מִי אַתָּה הַנָּעַר (Shmuel I 17:58) David understood the question, and answered with Beis HaLachmi, since Yishai was a man of war known for his might and the word carries both senses at once. Of the same sense are the days of youth, הִקְצַרְתָּ יְמֵי עֲלוּמָיו (Tehillim 89:46), You have shortened the days of his youth.

לְעֹלָם וָעֶד (Shemos 15:18), for ever and ever, and תְּשׁוּעַת עוֹלָמִים (Yeshayahu 45:17), which he reads as this world and the world to come, or else as long stretches of time, since the word is used of many days that are some part of the long עוֹלָם, world. וַעֲבָדוֹ לְעֹלָם (Shemos 21:6) is all the days until the Yovel; כִּי מֵעוֹלָם שָׁבַרְתִּי עֻלֵּךְ (Yirmiyahu 2:20) is from long ago; and לְעוֹלָם לֹא־אֶשְׁכַּח פִּקּוּדֶיךָ (Tehillim 119:93) is all the days of my life.

כפר.sense: To coat over, and from it the כַּפֹּרֶת; to remove, of anger and of sin, and so atonement; and further a village, a young lion, the frost, and golden pans.

more.t: אֲכַפְּרָה פָנָיו (Bereishis 32:21), I will take away his anger; לֹא תוּכְלִי כַּפְּרָהּ (Yeshayahu 47:11), you will not be able to remove it and annul it. Atonement is this same removing: וְכִפֶּר אַהֲרֹן (Shemos 30:10), by putting the blood on the horns of the mizbeach he removes the sins of Yisrael; and so the noun יוֹם כִּפֻּרִים (Vayikra 23:28).

more.h: What Chazal show of the word
more.t: Chazal in Kesubos say מִזְבֵּחַ מזיח מכפר, the mizbeach dislodges and atones, and ask whether the two are not one thing; the answer is מזיח גזירות, it dislodges decrees, מכפר עונות, it atones for sins. Both are language of removal, since מזיח is from וְלֹא יִזַּח הַחֹשֶׁן מֵעַל הָאֵפוֹד (Shemos 28:28), the choshen shall not come loose from the ephod. In that same way they say מכפר ליה בבליתא דפרסא, he takes off the fat and wipes it away with a coarse cloth.

אִישׁ כֹּפֶר נַפְשׁוֹ (Shemos 30:12), a man's ransom for his soul, which he glosses as the removing of his soul's sin, that is, his redemption; so too אִם כֹּפֶר יוּשַׁת עָלָיו (Shemos 21:30), if a ransom is laid upon him.

וּכְפַר הָעַמֹּנָי (Yehoshua 18:24), and נָלִינָה בַּכְּפָרִים (Shir HaShirim 7:12), let us lodge in the villages. The Targum renders הָעִיר וּבְנוֹתֶיהָ, the city and its outlying towns, with וְכַפְרָנָהָא, its villages, which are houses outside the city, for villagers and for men who work the land.

אֶשְׁכֹּל הַכֹּפֶר (Shir HaShirim 1:14) he takes as a plant which he names by its Arabic name, and so כְּפָרִים עִם נְרָדִים (Shir HaShirim 4:13). Some hold that כְּפָרִים עִם נְרָדִים is a different spice and not the same thing. Ibn Ezra wrote that אֶשְׁכֹּל הַכֹּפֶר is the cluster of the date palm, since the palm carries different names as its season changes, and it has a season whose Arabic name is this one, and it has a good scent.

more.h: The young lion, the frost, the pans
more.t: כְּפִיר אֲרָיוֹת (Shoftim 14:5) and הַכְּפִירִים שֹׁאֲגִים לַטָּרֶף (Tehillim 104:21), the young lions roaring for prey: these are the young in days among the lions and the wild beasts, and a כְּפִיר is bigger than a גּוּר, a cub. By way of figure, כְּפִיר גּוֹיִם נִדְמֵיתָ (Yechezkel 32:2) means their great and mighty one. Apart from these, דַּק כַּכְּפֹר עַל הָאָרֶץ (Shemos 16:14), fine as the frost on the ground, which falls at daybreak in the cold days; and וְלִכְפוֹרֵי הַזָּהָב (Divrei HaYamim I 28:17), כַּפּוֹת זָהָב, pans of gold, which Chazal in Zevachim took as basins, named so because the knife is wiped clean of blood on them.

שֹער.sense: To dread, and from it שְׂעָרָה, the storm; the שָׂעִיר, a he-goat, and the שְׂעִירִם; fine rain; hair, and a hairy man; and barley.

more.t: לֹא שְׂעָרוּם אֲבֹתֵיכֶם (Devarim 32:17) he reads as they did not dread them, that is, they did not fear them and did not serve them. The noun is the storm: בְּסוּפָה וּבִשְׂעָרָה דַּרְכּוֹ (Nachum 1:3), His way is in the whirlwind and in the storm.

שְׂעִיר עִזִּים (Bamidbar 7:16), a he-goat, is known. לַשְּׂעִירִם אֲשֶׁר הֵם זֹנִים אַחֲרֵיהֶם (Vayikra 17:7), the שְׂעִירִם after whom they stray, are the שֵׁדִים, the demons; they are called by this name because they are seen in the likeness of goats by those who believe in them.
כִּשְׂעִירִם עֲלֵי דֶשֶׁא (Devarim 32:2), which he glosses as the fine rain upon the grass.

more.h: Hair, the hairy man, and barley
more.t: שַׂעְרֵךְ כְּעֵדֶר הָעִזִּים (Shir HaShirim 4:1), your hair is like a flock of goats, which he reads as like the hair of a flock of goats; הֵן עֵשָׂו אָחִי אִישׁ שָׂעִר (Bereishis 27:11), Esav my brother is a hairy man; and וְהַפִּשְׁתָּה וְהַשְּׂעֹרָה (Shemos 9:31), the flax and the barley. The last two he calls known.

שׁער.sense: To reckon and estimate; שַׁעַר, a gate, and so the entrance of a whole land; and a second sense in שַׁעֲרוּרָה, which he leaves unglossed.

more.t: כְּמוֹ שָׁעַר בְּנַפְשׁוֹ כֶּן הוּא (Mishlei 23:7), as he reckons in his soul so is he; and in the plural מֵאָה שְׁעָרִים (Bereishis 26:12), a hundred measures, which he calls a matter of measure and estimate, and known. Some read שַׁעֲרוּרִיָּה in בְּבֵית יִשְׂרָאֵל רָאִיתִי (Hoshea 6:10), in the house of Yisrael I have seen, from this sense: what I reckoned of them I saw in them.

שַׁמָּה וְשַׁעֲרוּרָה (Yirmiyahu 5:30) and רָאִיתִי שַׁעֲרוּרָה (Yirmiyahu 23:14) he sets down as another sense without saying what it is, adding the form שַׁעֲרֻרִת (Yirmiyahu 18:13). Of כַּתְּאֵנִים הַשֹּׁעָרִים (Yirmiyahu 29:17), the foul figs, he does say what it is: an adjective, a matter of filth and foulness.

more.h: The gate, and the land's entrance
more.t: שַׁעַר הַשָּׁמָיִם (Bereishis 28:17), the gate of heaven, and from it the gatekeeper, שֹׁעֵר הָעִיר (Melachim II 7:10), the gatekeeper of the city. A whole land is called by its gate, after its entrance, as וְיִרַשׁ זַרְעֲךָ אֵת שַׁעַר אֹיְבָיו (Bereishis 22:17), your seed shall possess the gate of its enemies: a strong and fortified land is strong at its entrance, having mountains or seas about it, and once enemies have come in and passed those gates the whole land is taken before them. So פָּתוֹחַ נִפְתְּחוּ שַׁעֲרֵי אַרְצֵךְ (Nachum 3:13), the gates of your land are thrown wide open, and וְהֵצַר לְךָ בְּכָל שְׁעָרֶיךָ (Devarim 28:52), he will press you in all your gates.

קהל.sense: To gather, and to be gathered; the noun קָהָל, an assembly, with קְהִלָּה and מַקְהֵלִים for a gathering.

more.t: וַיִּקָּהֵל הָעָם עַל אַהֲרֹן (Shemos 32:1), the people gathered against Aharon, and הַנִּקְהָלִים עָלֶיךָ (Yechezkel 38:7), those gathered to you; where the verb takes an object, הַקְהֵל אֶת הָעָם (Devarim 31:12), assemble the people. The nouns are וְקָהָל וְעַם רָב (Yechezkel 26:7), an assembly and a great people, קְהִלַּת יַעֲקֹב (Devarim 33:4), the congregation of Yaakov, and בְּמַקְהֵלִים (Tehillim 26:12), in assemblies, with בְּמַקְהֵלוֹת (Tehillim 68:27) for the feminine plural.

In הַקָּהָל חֻקָּה אַחַת לָכֶם (Bamidbar 15:15) the heh is the heh of address, O assembly, one statute for you; the same heh as in הֶאָמוּר בֵּית יַעֲקֹב (Michah 2:7), O you who are called the house of Yaakov, and הַדּוֹר אַתֶּם רְאוּ (Yirmiyahu 2:31), O generation, see.

שׁמר.sense: To keep, to guard and to watch over; and by other senses the watches of the night, the lees of wine, שָׁמִיר, a hard stone, and שָׁמִיר, a thorn.

more.t: וְאָבִיו שָׁמַר אֶת הַדָּבָר (Bereishis 37:11), his father kept the matter, and וּשְׁמָרוֹ כְּרֹעֶה עֶדְרוֹ (Yirmiyahu 31:10), he will guard him as a shepherd guards his flock. It can also be a guarding that keeps others off: אֲנִי שָׁמַרְתִּי אָרְחוֹת פָּרִיץ (Tehillim 17:4) he reads as I watched the robber's paths so that no man should walk in them, and in the same way לִשְׁמֹר אֶת דֶּרֶךְ עֵץ הַחַיִּים (Bereishis 3:24).

וְרַק אַתֶּם שִׁמְרוּ מִן הַחֵרֶם (Yehoshua 6:18), only you, keep yourselves from the cherem: each man is to guard his fellow from it, for if one takes, all of them are punished, and that is why Yisrael were punished over Achan.

לֹא תִשְׁמוֹר עַל חַטָּאתִי (Iyov 14:16) can be that You watch only over my sin, the word carrying only, as אֵין טוֹב בָּאָדָם שֶׁיֹּאכַל (Koheles 2:24) means only that he eat; or that You will not wait, that is, You punish me at once and give me no time, as Chazal in Berachos say שמור לי על הפתח, wait for me at the door.

בְּאַשְׁמֹרֶת הַבֹּקֶר (Shemos 14:24), in the morning watch, and רֹאשׁ הָאַשְׁמֹרֶת הַתִּיכוֹנָה (Shoftim 7:19), the head of the middle watch; Chazal in Berachos say the night has three watches, and he holds that the pasuk in Shoftim bears it out. A city's watchman is named from this, since he is awake at night, guards the city and knows the hours. Of אָחַזְתָּ שְׁמֻרוֹת עֵינָי (Tehillim 77:5) he says it is as though You held the watches of my eyes so that they stay open and I do not sleep; Rabbi Moshe HaKohen takes שְׁמֻרוֹת in the first sense, as שׁוֹמְרוֹת, the eyelids that guard the eyes, which did not close.

וְשֹׁקֵט הוּא אֶל שְׁמָרָיו (Yirmiyahu 48:11), he rests on his lees, and הַקֹּפְאִים עַל שִׁמְרֵיהֶם (Tzefaniah 1:12), those congealed upon their lees. הִשָּׁמֵר וְהַשְׁקֵט (Yeshayahu 7:4) he reads here, settle on your lees in ease and quiet, and marks that it is accented on the last syllable, while everything in the sense of guarding is accented before it. Rav Saadiah Gaon read it instead as guarding: guard yourself from making war, and be quiet, do not fear.

more.h: שָׁמִיר, the hard stone and the thorn
more.t: כְּשָׁמִיר חָזָק מִצֹּר (Yechezkel 3:9), harder than flint, and מִצּוּר הַחַלָּמִישׁ (Devarim 8:15), which the Targum Yerushalmi renders שמרי טינרא, the shamir of the rock. Some read בְּצִפֹּרֶן שָׁמִיר (Yirmiyahu 17:1) as the hard iron, named so for its strength, as the hard rock is called שָׁמִיר. A second שָׁמִיר is a thorn: קוֹץ שָׁמִיר תַּעֲלֶה (Yeshayahu 32:13), which he reads as קוֹץ וְשָׁמִיר, thorn and brier, and שָׁמִיר וָשַׁיִת (Yeshayahu 9:17), a kind of thorn.

ארח.sense: אֹרַח, a way or path, and the verb taken from it; the wayfarer on it, the caravan that travels it, and a man's set meal.

more.t: וְאָרַח לְחֶבְרָה עִם פֹּעֲלֵי אָוֶן (Iyov 34:8), he keeps company with workers of iniquity, is the verb, and the noun it is taken from is אֹרַח, whose sense is דֶּרֶךְ, a way: וּכְאֹרַח אִישׁ יַמְצִאֶנּוּ (Iyov 34:11) and אָרְחִי וְרִבְעִי זֵרִיתָ (Tehillim 139:3). In the plural, חָדְלוּ אֳרָחוֹת (Shoftim 5:6) he glosses as those who pass along the ways ceased, and אֳרָחוֹת עֲקַלְקַלּוֹת stands in the same pasuk, crooked ways. On וְתִשְׁמוֹר כָּל אָרְחוֹתָי (Iyov 13:27), and You watch all my paths, he notes that Ben Asher reads it with a kamatz and Ben Naftali with a cholam.
לָאֹרֵחַ הַבָּא לוֹ (Shmuel II 12:4), the traveller who came to him: he is one going, עוֹבֵר אוֹרַח, passing along the way from place to place.
אֹרַח כַּנָּשִׁים (Bereishis 18:11) he glosses as the manner of women, and he brings כִּי דֶרֶךְ נָשִׁים לִי (Bereishis 31:35), for the way of women is upon me, as said in the same sense.

אֹרְחַת יִשְׁמְעֵאלִים (Bereishis 37:25), a caravan of Yishmaelim, which the Targum renders שְׁיָרַת עֲרָבָאֵי, a caravan of Arabians; so too אֹרְחוֹת דְּדָנִים (Yeshayahu 21:13). Because caravans are always going along the ways, they themselves were named for the ways.

וַאֲרֻחָתוֹ אֲרֻחַת תָּמִיד (Melachim II 25:30), which he glosses as his meal and his keep, and טוֹב אֲרֻחַת יָרָק (Mishlei 15:17), better a meal of herbs. These, he says, do not fall outside the first sense but are counted within it.

קדשׁ.sense: To be holy, and so to be set apart and forbidden to common use; and a second sense, to appoint or designate for a purpose.

more.t: פֶּן־ תִּקְדַּשׁ הַֽמְלֵאָה הַזֶּרַע (Devarim 22:9), lest the full yield of the seed be forfeit, he glosses as lest it become forbidden in benefit, the way what is consecrated is forbidden. Chazal in Kiddushin learn it from the same word in ואיש כי יקדיש את ביתו קדש, a man who consecrates his house: there the thing is forbidden in benefit, and so here.

וְאֶל־כָּל־מַֽאֲכָל הֲיִקְדָּשׁ (Chaggai 2:12) he glosses היטמא, will the food become tamei, forbidden by its tumah as consecrated food is forbidden; Chaggai was putting the laws of tumah to the kohanim, which they may have forgotten in the galus. Some of Chazal in Pesachim hold the kohanim erred in the answer, a fourth degree in kodesh being tamei; others that they erred in neither question; others that he asked about a fifth degree; others that he asked before a fourth degree in kodesh had been decreed. Radak holds the parsha shows they did not err, since throughout it he rebukes them over nothing but the building of the Beis.

כֹּל אֲשֶׁר־יִגַּע בִּבְשָׂרָהּ יִקְדָּשׁ (Vayikra 6:20): food that touches the flesh of the chatas and absorbs from it becomes holy as it is, and is eaten by whichever of the two laws is the stricter, so that shelamim flesh that touched a chatas is eaten for the chatas's day and night only. כָּל־הַנֹּגֵעַ בַּמִּזְבֵּחַ יִקְדָּֽשׁ (Shemos 29:37): even a korban already unfit that has gone up on the mizbeach is made fit by it, and once it has gone up it does not come down.

וְעָשׂוּ לִי מִקְדָּשׁ (Shemos 25:8), and they shall make Me a sanctuary; the house of holiness is the מִקְדָּשׁ. A king's palace is called so as well, כִּי מִקְדַּשׁ ־מֶלֶךְ הוּא (Amos 7:13), for it is like a mikdash, that none enter but those who are known there.

Some read מקדש at Yeshayahu 8:14 as a refuge, a place a man goes to be secure, and then לִשְׁנֵי בָתֵּי יִשְׂרָאֵל is one house for good and one for ill, Shevna and his party having made peace with the king of Ashur and Chizkiyahu and his party not. He offers another, that it is designation, a designation of punishment, a stumbling block set before them, as וְנָתַתִּי מִכְשׁוֹל לְפָנָיו (Yechezkel 3:20); on that reading the two houses are Pekach ben Remalyahu and Shevna's party, both of whom wanted the kingdom of Beis David to fall.

קַדְּשׁוּ ־צוֹם קִרְאוּ עֲצָרָה (Yoel 1:14), proclaim a fast, call an assembly, and קַדְּשׁוּ עָלֶיהָ מִלְחָמָה (Yirmiyahu 6:4), appoint war against her: these and their like are appointment. So too the קָדֵשׁ and the קְדֵשָׁה, לֹא־תִֽהְיֶה קְדֵשָׁה (Devarim 23:18), all of them being those appointed for lying with.

אמן.sense: To believe and to trust; and further, to be firm and enduring, to rear a child, and the אָמָּן, the master of a craft.

more.t: לְמַעַן יַֽאֲמִינוּ (Shemos 4:5), that they may believe. All such forms are trust and acceptance, קרידינצא in his own vernacular, credence; and they come out of אֱמוּנָה, since one who believes a thing gives it credence and holds it true.

In his own view אֱמֶת belongs to this root, its proper form being אֱמֶנֶת on the pattern of דְּבֶֽלֶת, the nun having fallen away for ease as it fell from בת, whose proper form is בֶּֽנֶת; the dagesh it takes when suffixes are joined to it proves as much, and its plural is formed as בנות is.

וְאָמַר כָּל־הָעָם אָמֵֽן (Devarim 27:17) is, it is true that whoever transgresses one of these shall be cursed, said either as a prayer or as acceptance, that they took the curse upon themselves should they transgress. So וְגַם־ אָמְנָה אֲחֹתִי בַת־אָבִי (Bereishis 20:12), it is true that she is my sister, my father's daughter.

A second strand of the root is standing firm. וְנֶֽאְמַן בֵּיתְךָ וּמַמְלַכְתְּךָ (Shmuel II 7:16), your house shall be established; יָתֵד בְּמָקוֹם נֶאֱמָן (Yeshayahu 22:23), a peg in a lasting place; מַכּוֹת גְּדֹלֹת וְנֶאֱמָנוֹת (Devarim 28:59), blows great and lasting; וַיְהִי יָדָיו אֱמוּנָה (Shemos 17:12), his hands held steady, and they did not let them down until the sun came in. אֲנַחְנוּ כֹּֽרְתִים אֲמָנָה (Nechemiah 10:1) is a binding covenant, and וְאֶת־ הָאֹמְנוֹת אֲשֶׁר צִפָּה חִזְקִיָּה (Melachim II 18:16) are the pillars that held the building up, which Yonasan renders וְיַת סְקוֹפַיָא, the thresholds of the gates.

כַּֽאֲשֶׁר יִשָּׂא הָֽאֹמֵן אֶת־הַיֹּנֵק (Bamidbar 11:12) is the one who rears him; וַתִּשָּׂאֵהוּ אֹֽמַנְתּוֹ (Shmuel II 4:4), his nurse; הָאֱמֻנִים עֲלֵי תוֹלָע (Eichah 4:5), those brought up on scarlet; וְאֶל־ הָאֹֽמְנִים אַחְאָב (Melachim II 10:1), those who reared him from his youth and were the men of his counsel, in whose charge the affairs of the kingdom lay. Here his father puts בָּנִים לֹֽא־ אֵמֻן בָּֽם (Devarim 32:21), that there is no breeding in them, a perverse generation who do evil when they are done good, as וַיִּשְׁמַן יְשֻׁרוּן וַיִּבְעָט (Devarim 32:15); Radak had taken those words above as children who do not believe, or in whom there is no truth.

more.h: Where he differs from Rabbi Yonah
more.t: Rabbi Yonah brought מֵסִיר שָׂפָה לְנֶאֱמָנִים (Iyov 12:20) into this root. Radak holds it is from נאם and of that sense, וַיִּנְֽאֲמוּ נְאֻֽם (Yirmiyahu 23:31), which is speaking, the closing nun added as the mark of an adjective, as in רחמן and נעמן; men clear in their tongue who know the wisdom of speech are called נאמנים.

שֹלם.sense: שַׂלְמָה, a garment: the letters of שִֹמְלָה turned about.

more.t: One line, on עַל־שֶׂה עַל־ שַׂלְמָה (Shemos 22:8), over a sheep, over a garment.

שׁלם.sense: To repay and requite; also to be complete and finished; and to be at peace, with שָׁלוֹם for peace.

more.t: יְשַׁלְּמוּנִי רָעָה תַּחַת טוֹבָה (Tehillim 35:12), they repay me evil for good; שַׁלֵּם יְשַׁלֵּם שׁוֹר תַּחַת הַשּׁוֹר (Shemos 21:36), he shall surely pay ox for ox. The nouns are בָּאוּ יְמֵי הַשִּׁלֻּם (Hoshea 9:7), the days of requital have come, וְשִׁלֻּמַת רְשָׁעִים תִּרְאֶֽה (Tehillim 91:8), and לִי נָקָם וְשִׁלֵּם (Devarim 32:35); all of them are recompense and payment.

כִּי לֹֽא־ שָׁלֵם עֲוֹן הָֽאֱמֹרִי עַד־הֵֽנָּה (Bereishis 15:16), the sin of the Emori is not yet full; וְשָֽׁלְמוּ יְמֵי אֶבְלֵֽךְ (Yeshayahu 60:20), the days of your mourning shall be ended; וַתִּשְׁלַם כָּל־הַמְּלָאכָה (Melachim I 7:51), all the work was finished. אֶבֶן שְׁלֵמָה (Devarim 25:15) is a full weight, and אֲבָנִים שְׁלֵמוֹת (Devarim 27:6) are whole stones that have not been cut. הָגְלָת שְׁלוֹמִֽים (Yirmiyahu 13:19) is that all of them went into exile, and on the same footing his father read מוּסַר שְׁלוֹמֵנוּ (Yeshayahu 53:5) as the chastisement of all of us.

שְֽׁלֵמִים הֵם אִתָּנוּ (Bereishis 34:21), they are at peace with us; הֲשָׁלוֹם אֲבִיכֶם הַזָּקֵן (Bereishis 43:27), is your aged father well. אִם־גָּמַלְתִּי שׁוֹלְמִי רָע (Tehillim 7:5) is, did I repay evil to one who was at peace with me. Where the verb takes an object it is to make peace: כִּֽי־ הִשְׁלִימָה אֶת־יְהוֹשֻׁעַ (Yehoshua 10:4), and גַּם־אוֹיְבָיו יַשְׁלִם אִתּֽוֹ (Mishlei 16:7), He makes even a man's enemies to be at peace with him.

more.h: Why the שְׁלָמִים is so called
more.t: Of the עולה everything goes up whole and the hide to the kohanim; of the chatas and the asham the blood and the eimurim go to the mizbeach and the breast and thigh to the kohanim; but of זֶבַח שְׁלָמִים (Vayikra 3:1) the blood and the eimurim go to the mizbeach, the breast and thigh to the kohanim, and the rest of the flesh and the hide to the owners, so that this zevach is peace between them all, as the Sifra sets it out. For the same reason it is called מִלּוּאִים, כִּי אֵיל מִלֻּאִים הֽוּא (Shemos 29:22), because it filled the desire of all of them, all of them eating from it.
שׁוּבִי שׁוּבִי הַשּׁוּלַמִּית (Shir HaShirim 7:1) is she who dwells in Yerushalayim, which is called שָׁלֵם.

ראה.sense: To see, and so to perceive and understand; with מַרְאֶה, a sight or a vision, and רֹאֶה, the one who sees, the navi.

more.t: וְלִבִּי רָאָה הַרְבֵּה חָכְמָה וָדָֽעַת (Koheles 1:16), my heart saw much wisdom and knowledge. So וַיַּרְא יַֽעֲקֹב כִּי יֶשׁ־שֶׁבֶר (Bereishis 42:1): he saw that the people of the land were going to Mitzrayim to buy grain, or he saw in his heart, that is, he understood from what he had heard and seen. הַדּוֹר אַתֶּם רְאוּ (Yirmiyahu 2:31) is, give your mind to the word of Hashem, and רְאֵה דְבָרֶיךָ טוֹבִים וּנְכֹחִים (Shmuel II 15:3) is, give your mind and understand.

more.h: The other senses lent to sight
more.t: Because the eye's perception is greater than the rest, the other senses are spoken of as seeing: וְכָל־הָעָם רֹאִים אֶת־הַקּוֹלֹת (Shemos 20:18), all the people saw the sounds, and רְאֵה רֵיחַ בְּנִי (Bereishis 27:27), see the smell of my son.

שָׁגוּ בָּֽרֹאֶה (Yeshayahu 28:7) he takes as, they erred in prophecy; his father read it as, they erred in a thing plain to every man. Rabbi Yaakov ben Elazar wrote that רואה is a noun of seeing and that אַֽחֲרֵי רֹאִֽי (Bereishis 16:13) is after my prophecy, and Radak says it is right; earlier in the entry he had read those words of the One seen by him, who saw him in his affliction.

לֹֽא־ אֶרְאֶה (Yeshayahu 38:11) Rav Saadiah Gaon explained in the sense of thanksgiving, and Radak says it is right, since to see the Creator is to give thanks and praise before Him and to consider His ways.

Some read הֵמָּה יַבִּיטוּ יִרְאוּ ־בִֽי (Tehillim 22:18), they look, they stare at me, as contempt, and so לְרַֽאֲוָה בָֽךְ (Yechezkel 28:17). He holds there is no need to take them out of their own sense, and brings Targum Yonasan, who renders לְרַֽאֲוָה בָֽךְ as לְאִסְתַכְּלָא בָךְ, to look at you.

וְהֵסִיר אֶת־ מֻרְאָתוֹ בְּנֹֽצָתָהּ (Vayikra 1:16) is the bird's crop, as the Targum has it; וְשַׂמְתִּיךְ כְּרֹֽאִי (Nachum 3:6) is filth and defilement. Of וְהָֽרָאָה וְאֶת־הָאַיָּה (Devarim 14:13) Chazal in Chullin say that רָאָה is דָּאָה, and that it is named רָאָה because it sees further than others.

עלה.sense: To go up and to rise; by a second sense, to be cut off and to cease; and from it עֹלָה, the offering that goes up whole, עֲלִיָּה, an upper room, and עָלֶה, a leaf.

more.t: עָלִיתָ לַמָּרוֹם (Tehillim 68:19), You went up on high; וְעָלָה הַגְּבוּל (Yehoshua 15:8), the border goes up; וּבָשָׂר עָלָה (Yechezkel 37:8), flesh came up over the sinews and the bones; כִּי עָלָה הַשָּׁחַר (Bereishis 32:26), the brightness of the day has come up. מִֽלְמַֽעֲלֵה הֶחָֽרֶס (Shoftim 8:13) he reads as the rising of the sun's brightness; Targum Yonasan has עַד לָא מֵעַל שִׁמְשָׁא, before the sun set, and on that reading the word means while the sun was still up, seen in the sky and not yet gone under the earth.

עֹלָה הוּא אִשֵּׁה רֵיחַ נִיחֹחַ (Vayikra 1:13). The korban is called so because it went up whole upon the mizbeach. שֹׂנֵא גָזֵל בְּעוֹלָה (Yeshayahu 61:8) is, if a man brings before Me an olah that was stolen I hate it, as וַֽהֲבֵאתֶם גָּזוּל (Malachi 1:13).

more.h: The other sense, being cut off
more.t: יְצוּעִי עָלָֽה (Bereishis 49:4), from the day you profaned it my couch was cut off; שֻׁדַּד מוֹאָב וְעָרֶיהָ עָלָה (Yirmiyahu 48:15); וַתַּעַל שִׁכְבַת הַטָּל (Shemos 16:14); אַֽל־ תַּֽעֲלֵנִי בַּֽחֲצִי יָמָי (Tehillim 102:25), do not cut me off in the midst of my days. Some read וְעָֽלְתָה יָדוֹ עַל־יַד רֵעֵֽהוּ (Zechariah 14:13) so, that the hand is torn away, and Targum Yonasan has וְתִתְּלַשׁ יְדֵיהּ. Some read וְהַבַּיִת הַזֶּה יִֽהְיֶה עֶלְיוֹן (Melachim I 9:8) of cutting off and ruin too; he holds there is no need to take it out of the first sense, and reads it as, this house which is now high, when they sin every passer by will be appalled and hiss.

more.h: Rooms above, steps, and the hours
more.t: וַיָּסַר אֶל־ הָֽעֲלִיָּה (Melachim II 4:11) and עֲלִיַּת ־קִיר (Melachim II 4:10) are the upper chamber, so called because it is over the house and a man goes up to it, and וְלֹא־תַֽעֲלֶה בְמַֽעֲלֹת (Shemos 20:23) are steps, because a man goes up on them. צֵל הַֽמַּֽעֲלוֹת (Yeshayahu 38:8) Targum Yonasan renders טוּל אֶבֶן שְׁעַיָא, which is the אבן השעות of the Mishnah in Keilim, the stone marked so as to know the hours of the day.

He writes עַל under this root, from the first sense: עֲלֵֽי ־עָשׂוֹר וַֽעֲלֵי ־נָבֶל (Tehillim 92:4), and without the yud of the plural עַל ־פְּנֵי הַמָּֽיִם (Bereishis 1:2). It comes in the sense of with: וַיָּבֹאוּ הָֽאֲנָשִׁים עַל ־הַנָּשִׁים (Shemos 35:22), the men came with the women. It comes in the sense of beside: וְזָֽבַחְתָּ עָלָיו אֶת־עֹֽלֹתֶיךָ (Shemos 20:21), beside it, for he did not slaughter upon the mizbeach, and חֹנִים עַל ־הַיָּם (Shemos 14:9), by the sea. It stands for אל: וַיֵּלֶךְ אֶלְקָנָה הָֽרָמָתָה עַל ־בֵּיתוֹ (Shmuel I 2:11), to his house; and for the letter beis: הִמָּלֵט עַל ־נַפְשֶׁךָ (Bereishis 19:17), which he reads as בנפשך, with your life.

וְהִנֵּה עֲלֵה ־זַיִת טָרָף בְּפִיהָ (Bereishis 8:11) and וַֽיִּתְפְּרוּ עֲלֵה תְאֵנָה (Bereishis 3:7) are the leaf; of וְהָבִיאוּ עֲלֵי ־זַיִת (Nechemiah 8:15) he says the branches together with the leaves are meant. His father read הִצִּית אֵשׁ עָלֶיהָ (Yirmiyahu 11:16) as on its leaves, and Dunash read פֶּן יִפְקֹד עָלֶיהָ (Yeshayahu 27:3) from this, that not even the leaf should be missing, still less the fruit.

קדם.sense: Before, in time and in place: קֶדֶם, ancient time, and the east; and to go before a thing, or to meet it.

more.t: מִימֵי קֶדֶם (Yeshayahu 23:7) and וּמֵרֹאשׁ הַרֲרֵי קֶדֶם (Devarim 33:15), with the adjective מְשַׁל הַקַּדְמֹנִי (Shmuel I 24:13), the proverb of the ancients, and בְּיָמִים קַדְמוֹנִים (Yechezkel 38:17).

עַל כֵּן קִדַּמְתִּי לִבְרֹחַ תַּרְשִׁישָׁה (Yonah 4:2), and אֲשֶׁר לֹא קִדְּמוּ אֶתְכֶם בַּלֶּחֶם וּבַמַּיִם (Devarim 23:5), they did not meet you with bread and water. Rabbi Yonah divides these into two senses; Radak holds there is no need, since to present oneself before a thing is itself to go before it. קַדְּמָה פָנָיו הַכְרִיעֵהוּ (Tehillim 17:13) he reads as, come before him in Your anger and bring him down.

The eastern quarter is called קֶדֶם, as the western is called אָחוֹר, behind: גַּן בְּעֵדֶן מִקֶּדֶם (Bereishis 2:8) and הֵן קֶדֶם אֶהֱלֹךְ (Iyov 23:8). קֵדְמָה מִזְרָחָה (Shemos 27:13) says it twice to make it plain, he notes, since מזרח is the better known word of the two, as נֶגְבָּה תֵימָנָה does. The east wind is קָדִים, and the eastern sea הַיָּם הַקַּדְמֹנִי (Yoel 2:20).

עור.sense: To wake and to rouse; and by other senses an enemy, uncovering, עוֹר, skin, and עִוֵּר, blind.

more.t: עוּרִי עוּרִי דְּבוֹרָה (Shoftim 5:12), awake, awake, Devorah, and the adjective אֲנִי יְשֵׁנָה וְלִבִּי עֵר (Shir HaShirim 5:2), I sleep but my heart is awake. Where the verb takes an object it is to rouse another: הֵעִיר, as of the spirit of כּוֹרֶשׁ מֶלֶךְ פָּרַס (Ezra 1:4 in his edition). On אָעִירָה שָּׁחַר (Tehillim 57:9) Rabbi Moshe HaKohen holds the verb carries an object, the sense being that he rouses the dawn.

וְהוּא עוֹרֵר אֶת חֲנִיתוֹ (Shmuel II 23:18) and אִם תָּעִירוּ (Shir HaShirim 2:6 in his edition). Rabbi Yonah brings עַרְעֵר תִּתְעַרְעַר (Yirmiyahu 51:58) here, the nations shaking and moving to and fro, and reads עִיר וּבֶהָלוֹת (Yirmiyahu 15:8) as tumult and stirring, which Radak calls a good explanation.

more.h: A word he reads from Chazal
more.t: On זַעֲקַת שֶׁבֶר יְעֹעֵרוּ (Yeshayahu 15:5) others read the letters as transposed, or as a doubled form of rousing. His own view is that it is a word of breaking, from what Chazal say in Sotah, מערערין אותה, that a sotah who refuses to drink is broken and beaten.

וַיְהִי עָרֶךָ (Shmuel I 28:16), which he glosses as your enemy and your foe, and וּמָלְאוּ פְנֵי תֵבֵל עָרִים (Yeshayahu 14:21), where Yonasan renders enemies. He allows the plain reading there too, cities, since the pasuk says וְעָרָיו הָרָס. On נָשֻׂא לַשָּׁוְא עָרֶיךָ (Tehillim 139:20) Rabbi Moshe HaKohen holds עריך stands for Your name, so that the sense is: Your name is borne in vain in their mouth.

פְּשֹׁטָה וְעֹרָה (Yeshayahu 32:11) and לְמַעַן הַבִּיט עַל מְעוֹרֵיהֶם (Chavakuk 2:15), whose sense is baring and uncovering. עוֹר is skin, כָּתְנוֹת עוֹר (Bereishis 3:21). And עִוֵּר is blind, אוֹ פִקֵּחַ אוֹ עִוֵּר (Shemos 4:11).

more.h: The blind and the lame at Yerushalayim
more.t: הַעִוְרִים וְהַפִּסְחִים (Shmuel II 5:6) he takes as images of bronze, and brings the beraisa of Rabbi Eliezer: the men of Yevus held Avraham's oath that his seed should not inherit their city, wrote it on bronze images and set them in the street, and told David he could not enter until he removed them. The Ibn Ezra reads it otherwise, that if we remove the blind and the lame to fight you they will keep you out, so strong is our building; and Yonasan renders the words as the sinful and the guilty.

שֹדר.sense: One citation only, וּשְׂדֵרֹת בָּֽאֲרָזִֽים (Melachim I 6:9), and a note that he has already explained the word in the section of samech.

more.t: Two clauses and no more: the phrase וּשְׂדֵרֹת בָּֽאֲרָזִֽים (Melachim I 6:9), and his word that he has already explained it in the section of samech. The sense itself is not set down here at all.

זבח.sense: To slaughter a sacrifice and offer it; from it זֶבַח, the sacrifice itself, and מִזְבֵּחַ, the place on which sacrifices are offered.

more.t: אֲשֶׁר תִּזְבַּח בָּעֶרֶב (Devarim 16:4), what you slaughter at evening, and זְבַח לֵאלֹהִים תּוֹדָה (Tehillim 50:14), offer thanksgiving as a sacrifice. He marks the intensive form as well: זִבַּח אָמוֹן וַיַּֽעַבְדֵֽם (Divrei HaYamim II 33:22), he sacrificed to Amon and served them; לָהֶם אֲזַבֵּחַ וְיַעְזְרוּנִי (Divrei HaYamim II 28:23), to them I will sacrifice and they will help me; עַל־ רָאשֵׁי הֶהָרִים יְזַבֵּחוּ (Hoshea 4:13), on the tops of the mountains they sacrifice.

וַיִּזְבַּח יַֽעֲקֹב זֶבַח בָּהָר (Bereishis 31:54), Yaakov offered a sacrifice on the mountain, the noun taking a segol. For many, זְבָחִים שְׁלָמִים (Shemos 24:5), peace sacrifices; with a heh added, זִבְחָה; and the gathered form זְבָחוֹת, as וְיֵבֹשׁוּ מִזִּבְחוֹתָֽם (Hoshea 4:19), they will be shamed by their sacrifices.

more.h: Why the incense altar is a מזבח
more.t: The place on which the sacrifices are offered is the מִזְבֵּחַ. וְעָשִׂיתָ מִזְבֵּחַ מִקְטַר קְטֹרֶת (Shemos 30:1), and you shall make an altar for burning incense, is called a מזבח although no sacrifices were offered upon it, because the blood of the sacrifice was sprinkled on it once in the year.

במה.sense: Of the sense he says only that it is known; the entry is on whether the word is weak in its last letter or in its middle, and he holds it is the middle.

more.t: וַיִּקָּרֵא שְׁמָהּ בָּמָה (Yechezkel 20:29), its name was called Bamah; רַק הַבָּמוֹת לֹֽא־סָרוּ (Melachim II 12:4), only the high places were not removed; וּבָמוֹת עוֹלָם לְמֽוֹרָשָׁה (Yechezkel 36:2), the ancient high places for a possession; עַל־ בָּמֳותֵי אָרֶץ (Devarim 32:13), on the high places of the earth; אֶעֱלֶה עַל־ בָּמֳתֵי עָב (Yeshayahu 14:14), I will go up above the heights of the cloud; and עַל־ בָּֽמוֹתֵימוֹ תִדְרֹֽךְ (Devarim 33:29), you will tread on their high places. Of all of them he says only ענינם ידוע, their sense is known.

more.h: Which letter of the root is weak
more.t: He filed the word among those weak in the final heh, as Rabbi Yonah wrote. Rabbi Yaakov ben Elazar filed it among those weak in the middle letter, because of the kamatz under the first root letter in the construct and with a suffix, as in קָמָה, standing grain, בְּקָמוֹת פְּלִשְׁתִּים (Shoftim 15:5), in the standing grain of the Pelishtim. That, he says, is the right one, and Rabbi Yonah himself wrote so in another place: better that במה be weak in its middle letter.

לאך.sense: A messenger, one who is sent, between men or from Hashem, and so the navi too; and in the same root מְלָאכָה, a man's work and what he owns.

more.h: The mem is not of the root
more.t: וּמַלְאָךְ בָּא אֶל־אִיּוֹב (Iyov 1:14), a messenger came to Iyov; וַיָּשׁוּבוּ הַמַּלְאָכִים (Bereishis 32:7), the messengers returned; מַלְאֲכֵי אֱלֹהִים (Bereishis 28:12). The mem of מלאך is one of the added letters. He writes all these words under this root because Rabbi Yonah wrote them so, holding the mem added; but it is possible, he says, that the mem is of the root and the words are of four letters.

וְלֹֽא־יִשָּׁמַע עוֹד קוֹל מַלְאָכֵֽכֵה (Nachum 2:14), the voice of your messengers will be heard no more. He takes it as מלאכיךָ, your messengers, a tzeirei standing under the kaf of the suffix in place of a kamatz and the heh like the heh of אֲשֶׁר־צִוִּיתִי אֹתָכָה (Shemos 29:35). Rabbi Yonah wrote that the heh stands in place of a yud, as מלאככִי, like שׁוּבִי נַפְשִׁי לִמְנוּחָיְכִי (Tehillim 116:7). Rabbi Yehudah ben Balaam wrote that it is the sound of the teeth eating the prey, as the pasuk says וְהִכְרַתִּי מֵאֶרֶץ טַרְפֵּךְ (Nachum 2:14), I will cut off your prey from the earth; and in the Persian tongue the millstones are called מלאככה, and they are the grinders, and the teeth are called grinders.

בְּמַלְֽאֲכוּת י"י (Chaggai 1:13), in the mission of Hashem, is the matter of being sent, whether between men or from the Creator. The navi is called a מלאך because he is the messenger of Hashem: וַיִּשְׁלַח מַלְאָךְ וַיֹּֽצִאֵנוּ מִמִּצְרָיִם (Bamidbar 20:16), He sent a messenger and brought us out of Mitzrayim, is Moshe Rabbeinu; so וַיֹּאמֶר חַגַּי מַלְאַךְ י"י (Chaggai 1:13), Chaggai the messenger of Hashem said, and וַיִּֽהְיוּ מַלְעִיבִים בְּמַלְֽאֲכֵי הָֽאֱלֹהִים (Divrei HaYamim II 36:16), they were mocking the messengers of Hashem. So too וַיַּעַל מַלְאַךְ ־י"י מִן־הַגִּלְגָּל (Shoftim 2:1), the messenger of Hashem went up from the Gilgal, and וַיְהִי כְּדַבֵּר מַלְאַךְ י"י אֶת־הַדְּבָרִים הָאֵלֶּה (Shoftim 2:4); in Vayikra Rabbah they said that this malach was Pinchas.

more.h: מְלָאכָה, work and what a man owns
more.t: Another matter in this root: מִכָּל־ מְלַאכְתּוֹ אֲשֶׁר עָשָֽׂה (Bereishis 2:2), from all His work which He had made. It falls on a man's doing, his money and his affairs. וְהַמְּלָאכָה הָֽיְתָה דַיָּם (Shemos 36:7), the work was enough for them, means the silver and the gold they brought and the rest of the things; לְרֶגֶל הַמְּלָאכָה (Bereishis 33:14), at the pace of the work, means the cattle; and so וְכָל־ הַמְּלָאכָה נְמִבְזָה וְנָמֵס (Shmuel I 15:9).

In the construct the aleph drops: לִמְלֶכֶת הַשָּׁמַיִם (Yirmiyahu 7:18), and so אִם־לֹא שָׁלַח יָדוֹ בִּמְלֶאכֶת רֵעֵֽהוּ (Shemos 22:7), if he has not put his hand to his fellow's goods, and in the absolute וְהַֽלְוִיִּם בַּמְלָֽאכֶת (Divrei HaYamim II 13:10), the Leviim at the work. The plural is מְלָאכוֹת, and in the construct the aleph moves, כֹּל מַלְֽאֲכוֹת הַתַּבְנִֽית (Divrei HaYamim I 28:19), all the works of the pattern, and לְסַפֵּר כָּל־ מַלְֽאֲכוֹתֶֽיךָ (Tehillim 73:28), to tell all Your works. But some read לִמְלֶכֶת הַשָּׁמַיִם with the mem as a root letter, from kingship, meaning the great star in the heavens, and Yonasan renders it לְכוֹכְבַת שְׁמַיָא, the star of the heavens.

אישׁ.sense: A man; the word takes in male and female together, is used even of what is not human, and is said of the great man, the head or master of a thing.

more.h: Man and woman, and the plurals
more.t: מַכֵּה אִישׁ וָמֵת (Shemos 21:12), one who strikes a man so that he dies, and אַשְׁרֵי־ אִישׁ יָרֵא אֶת־י"י (Tehillim 112:1), happy is the man who fears Hashem. איש takes in male and female alike; it is said of the male alone where a woman stands at his side, and without one where the sense of the pasuk shows it. The plural is אֲלֵיכֶם אִישִׁים אֶקְרָא (Mishlei 8:4), to you, O men, I call. The shin of אשה is doubled for the quiescent yud lost from איש, and in the construct it is lightened to אֵשֶׁת; sometimes אשת stands on its own, as כְּמוֹ אֵשֶׁת לֵדָֽה (Yirmiyahu 13:21), like a woman in labour. The plural of אשה is אִשֹּׁת הַזִּמָּֽה (Yechezkel 23:44), but נשים belongs to the root אנש and is written there.

more.h: Anything at all is called איש
more.t: Everything is called איש and אשה though it is not a man: of the keruvim, וּפְנֵיהֶם אִישׁ אֶל־אָחִיו (Shemos 25:20), their faces one toward another; of the curtains, אִשָּׁה אֶל־אֲחֹתָהּ (Shemos 26:3), one to another; of the stars, אִישׁ לֹא נֶעְדָּֽר (Yeshayahu 40:26), not one of them is missing; and of the beasts, אִישׁ וְאִשְׁתּוֹ (Bereishis 7:2), the male and his mate.

more.h: The great man, the master of a thing
more.t: גִּדְעוֹן בֶּן־יוֹאָשׁ אִישׁ יִשְׂרָאֵל (Shoftim 6:14) means the great one of Israel and its head; הֲלֽוֹא־ אִישׁ אַתָּה (Shmuel I 26:15) is, are you not a great man; י"י אִישׁ מִלְחָמָה (Shemos 15:3) is the great one and the master of war; אִם־תִּמְצְאוּ אִישׁ (Yirmiyahu 5:3) is a great man of good deeds, as the pasuk itself says before it, אִם־יֵשׁ עֹשֶׂה מִשְׁפָּט, if there is one who does justice. In גַּם־בְּנֵי אָדָם גַּם־בְּנֵי־ אִישׁ (Tehillim 49:3), בני אדם is said of the multitude and בני איש of the great. וְאִם־ אִישׁ שְׂפָתַיִם יִצְדָּֽק (Iyov 11:2) is the master of lips, the master of the tongue, who dresses his arguments in his best words.

אִם־ אִשׁ לְהֵמִין וּלְהַשְׂמִיל (Shmuel II 14:19) and עוֹד הַאִשׁ בֵּית רָשָׁע (Michah 6:10). Some say the aleph stands in place of a yud, so that the word is יש, there is, and Yonasan rendered אִם־אִשׁ לְהֵמִין as אִם אִית לְמִסְטֵי לְיַמִינָא. His father took אִשׁ as fire, with a chirik where אֵשׁ carries a tzeirei, bringing pairs of words that differ only in that vowel, and took עוֹד as in עוֹד יְֽהַלְלוּךָ סֶּֽלָה (Tehillim 84:5): all the days there will be fire in the house of the wicked, for the treasures of wickedness. He calls it well explained, save that the heh carries a patach and so looks to be the heh of a question. Rabbi Avraham took the words plainly, of a man: the honoured man of the city holds to his wickedness still after hearing the voice of the call, there being treasures of wickedness in his house. That reading he calls good too, save that it also does not answer to the patach.
וַיַּכּוּ אִישׁ אִישׁוֹ (Melachim I 20:20) means that each of them killed the one who came against him, and אִישׁוֹ there is the word with its suffix.

more.h: אִישׁוֹן, the pupil of the eye
more.t: כְּאִישׁוֹן עֵינֽוֹ (Devarim 32:10) is בת עינו, the pupil, called so because the form of a man is seen in it, which is why he joined אִישׁוֹן to בת and said שָׁמְרֵנִי כְּאִישׁוֹן בַּת־עָיִן (Tehillim 17:8), guard me as the pupil of the eye. His father wrote that אִישׁוֹן is said to make small, since the form appears small in the eye, and that the Hebrews add letters to make a thing small: שַׁבַּת שַׁבָּתוֹן (Vayikra 16:31), where שבת is said of the day itself from evening to evening and שבתון of the time added to it from the weekday to the holy; and הַֽאֲמִינוֹן אָחִיךְ (Shmuel II 13:20), where a letter is added to make the name small. Or the pupil is called so for its blackness, and in another measure, with the middle root letter fallen, בֶּאֱישׁוּן [ בֶּאֱשׁוּן ] חֹֽשֶׁךְ (Mishlei 20:20), in the blackness of darkness.

עיר.sense: A city, its plural sometimes showing the yud and sometimes hiding it; and a second matter in these letters, עַיִר, the donkey while it is still young.

more.t: וְאֵת אֲשֶׁר־ בָּעִיר (Bereishis 34:28), and what was in the city. The plural hides the yud in וַיִּתֶּן־אֹכֶל בֶּֽעָרִים (Bereishis 41:48), he put food in the cities, and עָרִים לָשָׁבֶת (Bamidbar 35:2), cities to dwell in; and shows it in וּשְׁלֹשִׁים עֲיָרִים לָהֶם (Shoftim 10:4), and they had thirty cities.

וְלֹא אָבוֹא בְּעִֽיר (Hoshea 11:9) he reads as a phrase whose sense is left unsaid: I will not come into another city, but into Yerushalayim. Rabbi Yonah wrote in the name of Rabbi Yitzchak ben Rabbi Shaul that it means, and if I do not come into a city, that is, that no place can hold Him; and this reading is needed because the pasuk says בְּקִרְבֵּךְ קְדוֹשׁ, the Holy One is in your midst.

וְעָרֶיהָ עָלָה (Yirmiyahu 48:15) comes in the masculine, and he explains it as each one of her cities after another being cut off. It may also be that the masculine is said of the people in the city.

more.h: עָר מוֹאָב, and the root עור
more.t: עָר מוֹאָב (Bamidbar 21:28) may be like עִיר, a city, or it may be the name of the city. וּמָֽלְאוּ פְנֵֽי־תֵבֵל עָרִֽים (Yeshayahu 14:21) and וְהִשְׁמַדְתִּי עָרֶֽיךָ (Michah 5:13) he has already explained, in two ways, under the root עור.

וְעַיִר פֶּרֶא אָדָם יִוָּלֵֽד (Iyov 11:12) he reads as וכעיר פרא, and like the colt of a wild ass; וְעַל־ עַיִר בֶּן־אֲתֹנֽוֹת (Zechariah 9:9), on a colt, the foal of she-asses; רֹֽכְבִים עַל־שְׁלֹשִׁים עֲיָרִים (Shoftim 10:4), riding on thirty colts; and with the middle root letter hidden, אֹֽסְרִי לַגֶּפֶן עִירֹה [ עִירוֹ ] (Bereishis 49:11), binding his colt to the vine. Its sense is the donkey while it is still small. The word fell on the פרא, the wild ass, as well, because the wild ass is like the donkey; but the wild ass is of the kind called chayah and the donkey of the kind called behemah, as Chazal said in Berachos 9b, כדי שיכיר בין חמור לערוד, that he may tell a donkey from an ערוד, and the ערוד is the פרא.

רגז.sense: To tremble and shake, whether out of fear or out of anger; and where the verb takes an object, to set another trembling.

more.t: וְרָגַז וְשָׂחַק וְאֵין נָֽחַת (Mishlei 29:9), he rages and he laughs and there is no quiet; וְרָֽגְזוּ וְחָלוּ (Devarim 2:25), they will tremble and be in anguish; וַתִּרְגַּז בִּטְנִי (Chavakuk 3:16), my belly trembled, and וְתַחְתַּי אֶרְגָּז (Chavakuk 3:16), and I tremble where I stand; מֽוֹסְדוֹת הַשָּׁמַיִם יִרְגָּזוּ (Shmuel II 22:8), the foundations of the heavens shake; and אַֽל־ תִּרְגְּזוּ בַּדָּֽרֶךְ (Bereishis 45:24). The sense he gives is trembling and movement, out of fear or out of anger.

חָדְלוּ רֹגֶז (Iyov 3:17), they have ceased from trembling; מֵֽעָצְבְּךָ וּמְֽרָגְזֶךָ (Yeshayahu 14:3), from your sorrow and from your trembling, where the serving mem takes a chirik; and with the feminine heh, וּמֵימֶיךָ בְּרָגְזָה וּבִדְאָגָה תִּשְׁתֶּֽה (Yechezkel 12:18), you will drink your water in trembling and in worry.

וַתִּרְגְּזִי ־לִי בְּכָל־אֵלֶּה (Yechezkel 16:43) is the verb taking an object. So וְהִרְגִּיז לְיֹֽשְׁבֵי בָבֶֽל (Yirmiyahu 50:34), he will set the dwellers of Bavel trembling; הַמַּרְגִּיז אֶרֶץ מִמְּקוֹמָהּ (Iyov 9:6), who shakes the earth out of her place; and לָמָּה הִרְגַּזְתַּנִי לְהַֽעֲלוֹת אֹתִי (Shmuel I 28:15), why have you disturbed me to bring me up. Of a man turning it on himself, יַעַן הִתְרַגֶּזְךָ אֵלַי (Yeshayahu 37:29).

On וְאֵת הִֽתְרַגֶּזְךָ אֵלָֽי (Yeshayahu 37:28) Rabbi Yonah wrote that the word may fall on the sound of thunder and quaking, and that what is wanted here is your pressing upon Me with words and making your tongue great against Me. What holds this up is וְשַֽׁאֲנַנְךָ עָלָה בְאָזְנָי (Yeshayahu 37:28), which is to say the abundance of your words; and of this sense too is וַתִּרְגְּזִי־לִי בְּכָל־אֵלֶּה, you did much in all these deeds.
תָּשִׂימוּ בָֽאַרְגַּז מִצִּדּוֹ (Shmuel I 6:8). He does not treat the word here, having written it in the section of aleph among the words of four letters.

אנף.sense: To be angry. אף, anger, is of this same root and this same sense, its nun dropping out before the pronoun; and the אנפה is a bird.

more.t: כִּי אָנַפְתָּ בִּי (Yeshayahu 12:1), for You were angry with me, and פֶּן־ יֶאֱנַף וְתֹאבְדוּ דֶרֶךְ (Tehillim 2:12), lest He be angry and you perish in the way. Where a man turns his anger on another, גַּם־בִּי הִתְאַנַּף (Devarim 1:37), He was angry with me too. ענין כעס, a sense of anger.

ואף הוא מזה השרש והענין, af too is of this root and this sense. Joined to the pronoun it is אַפּוֹ, אַפִּי, אַפְּךָ, his anger, my anger, your anger, the dagesh standing in for the nun that has fallen away. He says he writes on it again at its own root.
הָֽאֲנָפָה לְמִינָהּ (Vayikra 11:19) is the name of a bird, and Chazal (Chullin 63a) say אנפה זו דיה רגזנית, the anafah is the quarrelsome dayah.

עצב.sense: Vexation and grief; then the toil that wearies a man; and idols, called עצבים, since a man vexes himself with them and vexes Hashem by them.

more.t: וְלֹֽא־ עֲצָבוֹ אָבִיו (Melachim I 1:6), his father never vexed him, which he glosses לא הרגיזו ולא הדאיגו, he did not anger him and did not trouble him. Standing without an object, וַֽעֲצוּבַת רוּחַ (Yeshayahu 54:6), grieved in spirit, and וְעָשִׂיתָ מֵֽרָעָה לְבִלְתִּי עָצְבִּי (Divrei HaYamim I 4:10), which he reads as a prayer that He deal with him so that he not be grieved and not be anxious from evil. So נֶעְצַב אֶל־דָּוִד (Shmuel I 20:34), וְעַתָּה אַל־ תֵּעָצְבוּ (Bereishis 45:5), now do not be grieved, and וַיִּתְעַצֵּב אֶל־לִבּֽוֹ (Bereishis 6:6).

more.h: Where the verb takes an object
more.t: וְהֵמָּה מָרוּ וְעִצְּבוּ אֶת־רוּחַ קָדְשׁוֹ (Yeshayahu 63:10), they rebelled and vexed His holy spirit, which he glosses הרגיזו והדאיגו, they angered it and troubled it; כָּל־הַיּוֹם דְּבָרַי יְעַצֵּבוּ (Tehillim 56:6), and יַֽעֲצִיבוּהוּ בִּֽישִׁימֽוֹן (Tehillim 78:40), they grieved Him in the wasteland.

more.h: The nouns, and one borrowed word
more.t: עֶצֶב in וְלֹֽא־יוֹסִף עֶצֶב עִמָּֽהּ (Mishlei 10:22) and וּדְבַר־ עֶצֶב יַֽעֲלֶה־אָֽף (Mishlei 15:1); לְמַֽעֲצֵבָה תִּשְׁכָּבֽוּן (Yeshayahu 50:11); קֹרֵֽץ עַיִן יִתֵּן עַצָּבֶת (Mishlei 10:10) and in construct וּבְעַצְּבַת ־לֵב רוּחַ נְכֵאָֽה (Mishlei 15:13); in the plural יָגֹרְתִּי כָל־ עַצְּבֹתָי (Iyov 9:28) and וּמְחַבֵּשׁ לְעַצְּבוֹתָֽם (Tehillim 147:3). ענין כלם הרוגז והדאגה, all of them vexation and worry. מְחַבֵּשׁ, binding up, is said of worry על דרך השאלה, as borrowed speech, since that very pasuk says הָרוּפֵא לִשְׁבוּרֵי לֵב, who heals the broken of heart.

more.h: Three ways to read one line
more.t: אִם־דֶּֽרֶךְ־ עֹצֶב בִּי (Tehillim 139:24) he reads as: if there is in me a way of vexation and worry over what befalls me, though in truth he takes it all with love; or if I am walking an evil way that angers and vexes You; and once he has brought the idols, that the line may mean if I am turning to the עצבים, the idols.

From this sense the images of avodah zarah are called עצבים, as הַעֶצֶב נִבְזֶה, the despised idol, and פֶּן־תֹּאמַר עָצְבִּי עָשָׂם, lest you say my idol did them; כי הם דאגה ורוגז, for they are worry and vexation to busy oneself with, and a man vexes Hashem by them. עָשִׂינוּ לָהּ כַּוָּנִים לְהַעֲצִבָה (Yirmiyahu 44:19) is to make her idols; or else לְהַעֲצִבָה stands in for the word meant, לשמחה, to gladden her, and its ה is soft where the rule would give it a mappiq.

מַסִּיעַ אֲבָנִים יֵֽעָצֵב בָּהֶם (Koheles 10:9), he wears and wearies himself with them; יָדֶיךָ עִצְּבוּנִי (Iyov 10:8), Your hands toiled and laboured in forming me, said as a figure, while Rabbi Moshe ben Ezra takes it from the sinews, which are called עצבים. So בְּעִצָּבוֹן תֹּֽאכֲלֶנָּה (Bereishis 3:17) and עִצְּבוֹנֵךְ וְהֵֽרֹנֵךְ (Bereishis 3:16), toil and weariness. And בְּכָל־ עֶצֶב יִהְיֶה מוֹתָר (Mishlei 14:23): in every toil a man toils there is gain and rank for him, since by much toil a man comes to rank and wealth and rule, while the toil of the lips and the weariness of talk bring only want, as the pasuk ends וּדְבַר־שְׂפָתַיִם אַךְ־לְמַחְסֽוֹר.

בהם.sense: A beast: a word for the kind at large and sometimes for one animal, and בְהֵמוֹת (Iyov 40:15) is a single beast that carries the name.

more.h: The ending, and a second form
more.t: זֹאת הַבְּהֵמָה אֲשֶׁר תֹּאכֵלוּ (Devarim 14:4) and בְּהֵמָה וָרֶמֶשׂ (Bereishis 1:24), where the ה is the mark of the feminine; in construct וְאֵת בֶּֽהֱמַת הַֽלְוִיִּם (Bamidbar 3:41), the cattle of the Leviim. But תַּחַת בְּהֶמְתָּם (Bamidbar 3:45) and בְּהֶמְתְּךָ לֹֽא־תַרְבִּיעַ כִּלְאַיִם (Vayikra 19:19) do not come from בהמה at all but from a form בְּהֶמֶת, which is nowhere found, since from בהמה one would say בְּהֵמָֽתְךָ and not בְּהֶמְתְּךָ. He refers the reader to his grammar, in the gate of nouns.

more.h: The kind, and the single animal
more.t: והוא שם כלל ופעם פרט, it is a word for the kind and sometimes for the one, as כִּי אִם־ הַבְּהֵמָה אֲשֶׁר אֲנִי רֹכֵב בָּֽהּ (Nechemiah 2:12), the one animal I was riding on.

הִנֵּה־נָא בְהֵמוֹת אֲשֶׁר־עָשִׂיתִי עִמָּךְ (Iyov 40:15) is בהמה אחת ששמה בהמות, one beast whose name is Behemos. Some say שְׁאַל־נָא בְהֵמוֹת וְתֹרֶךָּ (Iyov 12:7) is that same beast, since וְתֹרֶךָּ, and it will teach you, is said in the singular. He holds there is no need for that: וְתֹרֶךָּ means each and every one of the beasts, or it falls on the kind, as the same pasuk has וְעוֹף הַשָּׁמַיִם וְיַגֶּד־לָֽךְ, and the bird of the sky, and it will tell you.

בַּֽהֲמוֹת נֶגֶב (Yeshayahu 30:6). The navi foretold that the beasts of the Negev would come out to devour Yisrael as they went to seek help from Mitzrayim, carrying their wealth on the shoulders of young donkeys and their treasures on camels' humps to bribe Mitzrayim for aid, from a people who would not profit them. The beasts are the ones the pasuk itself names, לָבִיא וָלַיִשׁ מֵהֶם אֶפְעֶה וְשָׂרָף מְעוֹפֵף, lion and lioness, viper and flying serpent. Mitzrayim is called Negev because it lies south of Eretz Yisrael; or נֶגֶב is the parched land, as אֶרֶץ הַנֶּגֶב נְתַתָּנִי (Shoftim 1:15), since wild beasts dwell in the wilderness and in the Negev.

נער.sense: To roar or bray; to shake out; and נַעַר, a youth, and so also a servant, whatever his years, since the young serve the older.

more.t: נָֽעֲרוּ כְּגוֹרֵי אֲרָיֹֽות (Yirmiyahu 51:38), which he glosses שאגו והמו, they roared and made their noise; and Chazal use the word of a donkey, חמור נוער (Berachos 3a), a donkey brays. Rabbi Yonah puts כִּי נֵעוֹר מִמְּעוֹן קָדְשֽׁוֹ (Zecharyah 2:17) in this root, a word of description on the pattern of יָכוֹל, able, save that the vowel changed because of the ayin, and so his father wrote, who said that the word is used of Hashem after the manner of מִצִּיּוֹן יִשְׁאָג (Yoel 4:16), He roars from Tzion.

גַּם־חָצְנִי נָעַרְתִּי (Nechemiah 5:10), I shook out my lap, and נֹעֵר כַּפָּיו מִתְּמֹךְ בַּשֹּׁחַד (Yeshayahu 33:15), shaking his palms clear of holding a bribe. וְנֹעֵר בָּשָׁן וְכַרְמֶֽל (Yeshayahu 33:9) is shaking off its fruit and its crop, or else the verb stands without an object. In the passive, נִנְעַרְתִּי כָּֽאַרְבֶּֽה (Tehillim 109:23), I am shaken off like a locust, and וְיִנָּֽעֲרוּ רְשָׁעִים מִמֶּֽנָּה (Iyov 38:13); with an object, וְנִעֵר פַּרְעֹה וְחֵילוֹ (Tehillim 136:15) and וַיְנַעֵר, and He shook out, of Mitzrayim (Shemos 14:27); and הִתְנַֽעֲרִי מֵעָפָר (Yeshayahu 52:2), shake yourself from the dust.

וְהָיָה הֶחָסֹן לִנְעֹרֶת (Yeshayahu 1:31), and in the Mishnah (Shabbos 4:1) בנעורת של פשתים, the tow of flax, which is what is shaken and beaten off the flax as it is dressed. Some read וְהַנַּעַר נָֽעַר (Shmuel I 1:24) from this, that the youth was sharp and knew good from bad, like one who shakes the chaff clear.

כִּי־ נַעַר אָנֹֽכִי (Yirmiyahu 1:6). One small in years is called נער, and because it is the way of the small to serve the great, the attendant is called נער even when he is old in years: נַעַר עִבְרִי (Bereishis 41:12), וְהוּא נַעַר אֶת־בְּנֵי בִלְהָה (Bereishis 37:2), גֵּיֽחֲזִי נַֽעֲרוֹ (Melachim II 4:12), בְּנַֽעֲרֵי שָׂרֵי הַמְּדִינוֹת (Melachim I 20:14). וּרְחַבְעָם הָיָה נַעַר (Divrei HaYamim II 13:7) is כנער בדעתו, a youth in his understanding. The least of the flock carries the name too, הַנַּעַר לֹֽא־יְבַקֵּשׁ וְהַנִּשְׁבֶּרֶת לֹא יְרַפֵּא (Zecharyah 11:16).

וְהַנַּעַר נָֽעַר (Shmuel I 1:24) he reads as the child being still a small child, twenty-four months old, since the pasuk says עד הִגָּמֵל הנער, until the youth was weaned, and a child is nursed until twenty-four months. His father read the same two words the other way, that he was big for his years, a youth grown larger than his age warranted.

more.h: Girls, and the days of youth
more.t: וְהַנַּֽעֲרָה יָפָה עַד־מְאֹד (Melachim I 1:4), נְעָרוֹת בְּתוּלוֹת (Esther 2:2), רִבְקָה וְנַֽעֲרֹתֶיהָ (Bereishis 24:61). For the time of life, רַבַּת צְרָרוּנִי מִנְּעוּרָי (Tehillim 129:2), they have afflicted me much from my youth, and מְגֻדָּלִים בִּנְעוּרֵיהֶם (Tehillim 144:12). תָּמֹת בַּנֹּעַר נַפְשָׁם (Iyov 36:14) is their soul dying in youth, though some take that one from the second sense, a hard death.

נגשֹ.sense: To press, drive and exact: the נֹגֵשׂ is the one who drives the people at their work and wrings payment from them. All of it a sense of pressure.

more.t: נָגַשׂ אֶת־הַכֶּסֶף וְאֶת־הַזָּהָב (Melachim II 23:35), he exacted the silver and the gold, לֹֽא־ יִגֹּשׂ אֶת־רֵעֵהוּ וְאֶת־אָחִיו (Devarim 15:2), he shall not press his fellow or his brother, וְכָל־עַצְּבֵיכֶם תִּנְגֹּֽשׂוּ (Yeshayahu 58:3), אֵיךְ שָׁבַת נֹגֵשׂ (Yeshayahu 14:4), how the oppressor has ceased, and וְהַנֹּֽגְשִׂים אָצִים (Shemos 5:13), the taskmasters pressing them on.

In the passive, וְנִגַּשׂ הָעָם אִישׁ בְּאִישׁ וְאִישׁ בְּרֵעֵהוּ (Yeshayahu 3:5), the people pressed one against another, כִּי נִגַּשׂ הָעָם (Shmuel I 13:6), and נִגַּשׂ וְהוּא נַֽעֲנֶה (Yeshayahu 53:7), pressed and himself afflicted. He brings יַעַן כִּי נִגַּשׁ הָעָם (Yeshayahu 29:13) here as well, a word he weighs again at the other root. כלם ענין לחץ, all of them a sense of pressure.

נגשׁ.sense: To draw near, and where the verb takes an object to bring near; the same word can tell a man to move off, since to leave one place is to come near another.

more.t: וַיִּגַּשׁ אֵלָיו יְהוּדָה (Bereishis 44:18), and Yehudah drew near to him, וַתִּגַּשְׁןָ הַשְּׁפָחוֹת (Bereishis 33:6), גְּשׁוּ ־נָא אֵלַי וַיִּגָּשׁוּ (Bereishis 45:4), draw near to me now, and they drew near, גּשִֽׁי הֲלֹם (Rus 2:14), עַד־ גִּשְׁתּוֹ עַד־אָחִֽיו (Bereishis 33:3), and with the pathach גַּשׁ פְּגַע־בּוֹ (Shmuel II 1:15), come near, strike him down.

more.h: Why it can mean move away
more.t: גְּשָׁה ־לִּי וְאֵשֵֽׁבָה (Yeshayahu 49:20) he glosses as move over yonder for my sake so that I may sit with room, since the place is too narrow for me. So too גֶּשׁ ־הָלְאָה (Bereishis 19:9), stand back: though the man is far from where the speaker stands, he is near to the other place, and the word is said of that nearness.

more.h: Whether one word has a sin or a shin
more.t: יַעַן כִּי נִגַּשׁ הָעָם הַזֶּה (Yeshayahu 29:13): so Rabbi Yonah wrote it, and so it stands in some of the sefarim. But one note of the Mesorah counts four places with a sin and gives their catchwords: וְאִישׁ יִשְׂרָאֵל, and the men of Yisrael (Shmuel I 13:6), with its fellow (Shmuel I 14:24), יִרְֽהֲבוּ, they shall be insolent (Yeshayahu 3:5), and נַֽעֲנֶה, afflicted (Yeshayahu 53:7). If those four are the whole tally, this word is with a shin; in some sefarim it is found with a sin all the same. The Targum's view fits the reading he gives here, since he rendered חֲלַף דְאִיתְרַבְרַב עַמָא הָדֵין, because this people has grown haughty.

וְנִגַּשׁ מֹשֶׁה לְבַדּוֹ (Shemos 24:2), Moshe alone shall come near, וְנִגְּשָׁה יְבִמְתּוֹ (Devarim 25:9), and וְגַם הַכֹּֽהֲנִים הַנִּגָּשִׁים (Shemos 19:22), the kohanim who come near. Where the verb takes an object, וְהִגִּישׁוֹ אֲדֹנָיו (Shemos 21:6), his master shall bring him near, and וַיַּגֶּשׁ ־לוֹ וַיֹּאכַל (Bereishis 27:25), he brought it to him and he ate. Rabbi Yonah holds לֹֽא־ תַגִּישׁ וְתַקְדִּים בַּֽעֲדֵינוּ הָֽרָעָֽה (Amos 9:10) has no object; he answers that it may be read with one like its fellows, that you will bring the enemies near and set them before us. In the passive, לֹֽא־לִנְחֻשְׁתַּיִם הֻגָּשׁוּ (Shmuel II 3:34).

תבה.sense: The ark, תֵּבָה, a word whose meaning is plain; where its root lies he and Rabbi Yonah differ.

more.t: צֵא מִן־ הַתֵּבָה (Bereishis 8:16), go out of the ark, and תֵּבַת עֲצֵי־גֹפֶר (Bereishis 6:14), an ark of gopher wood; the word, he says, is known. He allows that the root may be תיב, teiv, the noun then standing on the pattern of צֵידָה, provision, and שֵֹיבָה, grey age. But Rabbi Yonah wrote it under this root, on the pattern of לֶחֶם הַפֶּחָה (Nechemiah 5:18), the governor's bread.

חלץ.sense: To draw off and so to be parted: a shoe drawn off, a man drawn out of his trouble; and the loins, from which the man girded for war is called armed.

more.t: חָלַץ מֵהֶֽם (Hoshea 5:6), which he glosses חלק ונפרד וסר מהם, he parted and separated and turned away from them. On גַּם־תַּנִּין (Eichah 4:3), even the tannin, the verb חָלְצוּ is their drawing out their breasts and uncovering them to nurse their young. וְחָֽלְצָה נַֽעֲלוֹ (Devarim 25:9), she shall draw off his shoe and take it away, and where the verb is strengthened, וְחִלְּצוּ אֶת־הָאֲבָנִים (Vayikra 14:40), they shall take the stones out and pull them from their place.

Because a man puts these on by taking those off, a change of clothes carries the name: וְהַלְבֵּשׁ אֹֽתְךָ מַֽחֲלָצֽוֹת (Zecharyah 3:4), הַמַּֽחֲלָצוֹת וְהַמַּֽעֲטָפוֹת (Yeshayahu 3:22), וְקַח־לְךָ אֶת־ חֲלִֽצָתוֹ (Shmuel II 2:21), and וַיִּקַּח אֶת־ חֲלִיצוֹתָם (Shoftim 14:19), and he took their garments.

In this same sense, rescue: צַדִּיק מִצָּרָה נֶחֱלָץ (Mishlei 11:8), which he glosses נפרד וסר מהצרה, parted and removed from the trouble, and לְמַעַן יֵחָלְצוּן יְדִידֶיךָ (Tehillim 60:7). So חַלְּצָה נַפְשִׁי (Tehillim 6:5) and יְחַלְּצֵנִי כִּֽי־חָפֵֽץ בִּֽי (Tehillim 18:20). וָֽאֲחַלְּצָה צוֹרְרִי רֵיקָֽם (Tehillim 7:5) he reads as rather I rescued him: were I one who repaid his friend evil, I would still have delivered the man who is my enemy for nothing.

more.h: The loins, and the armed man
more.t: אֱזָר־נָא כְגֶבֶר חֲלָצֶיךָ (Iyov 38:3) and מֵֽחֲלָצֶיךָ יֵצֵֽאוּ (Bereishis 35:11) are הם המתנים, the loins, and from them וְעָבַר לָכֶם כָּל־ חָלוּץ (Bamidbar 32:21), every man girded with the gear of war at his loins, and נֵֽחָלֵץ חֻשִׁים (Bamidbar 32:17), הֵחָֽלְצוּ מֵֽאִתְּכֶם (Bamidbar 31:3). He denies that this last takes an object, as Rabbi Yonah wrote: it is as though it said let some of you be armed, the men and the mighty among you, and let them go against Midian. On this reckoning he offers that וקח לך את חליצתו may belong here as well, one man saying to another: take yourself one of the lads walking with me, that he may go back with you, and if you fear him take his weapons of war, and even so do not kill him.

וְעַצְמֹתֶיךָ יַֽחֲלִיץ (Yeshayahu 58:11) he takes otherwise, as ידשן, He will make fat, after שְׁמוּעָה טוֹבָה תְּדַשֶּׁן ־עָֽצֶם (Mishlei 15:30). In that sense Chazal said (Eruvin 39a) that one who goes before the teivah on Rosh Hashanah says והחליצנו, meaning satisfy us and make us fat with Your mitzvos; or they explained it as a word of rest, give us rest.

In Vayikra Rabbah, parashah 34, the word is used in four ways: ישלוף, to draw off, in וְחָֽלְצָה נַֽעֲלוֹ; ישזיב, to rescue, in חַלְּצֵנִי (Tehillim 140:2); יזיין, to arm, in חֲלוּצִים תַּֽעַבְרוּ (Devarim 3:18); and יניח, to give rest, in וְעַצְמֹתֶיךָ יַֽחֲלִיץ, as one says רצה והחליצנו.

אזן.sense: The ear, and to give ear; and from the same letters מאזנים, the scales, named in the dual because the instrument has two pans.

more.t: אֹֽזֶן ־אַֽהֲרֹן הַיְמָנִית (Vayikra 8:23), Aharon's right ear, הֲנֹטַע אֹזֶן הֲלֹא יִשְׁמָע (Tehillim 94:9), He who planted the ear, shall He not hear, and אָזְנַיִם כָּרִיתָ לִּי (Tehillim 40:7).

more.h: Why the ear is said to understand
more.t: הֲלֹא־ אֹזֶן מִלִּין תִּבְחָן (Iyov 12:11) and שָֽׁמְעָה אָזְנִי וַתָּבֶן לָֽהּ (Iyov 13:1). סמך הבחינה והתבונה והחנינה לאזן, ואינה אלא ללב: he attaches the weighing and the understanding and the favour to the ear, though they belong to the heart alone, לפי שהיא תחלת הפעולה, because the ear is where the act begins; and so with וַתְּאַשְּׁרֵנִי, and it called me fortunate. On the same footing he takes וּבִתְבוּנוֹת כַּפָּיו יַנְחֵֽם, and with the understanding of his hands he led them.

הַֽאֲזִינוּ הַשָּׁמַיִם (Devarim 32:1) is הטו אזן, incline the ear, and so every word of this sense in this root. Of the same are אָזִין עַד־תְּבוּנֹֽתֵיכֶם (Iyov 32:11), I give ear to your reasonings, and שֶׁקֶר מֵזִין עַל־לְשׁוֹן הַוֹּֽת (Mishlei 17:4), whose rule would be אַאֲזִין, מַאֲזִין.

more.h: The scales, and one disputed word
more.t: בְּמֹאזְנַיִם לַֽעֲלוֹת (Tehillim 62:10) and מֹאזְנֵי צֶדֶק אַבְנֵי־צֶדֶק (Vayikra 19:36) are the instrument one weighs with, called in the dual because it has two pans. On וְאִזֵּן וְחִקֵּר (Koheles 12:9) Rabbi Yonah ibn Janach explains from this sense, that he weighed one matter against another and searched them out, while Rabbi Yehudah put the word with the first sense, of hearing.

Rabbi Yonah wrote in one place that וְיָתֵד תִּהְיֶה לְךָ עַל־ אֲזֵנֶךָ (Devarim 23:14) is of this root. He holds the right account is that the א is added to the word and it means כלי זיניך, your weapons.

רחם.sense: To show mercy, and רַחֲמִים, mercies; רֶחֶם, the womb; and הָרָחָמָה, a bird said to pity its young greatly.

more.t: רַחֵם אֲרַחֲמֶנּוּ (Yirmiyahu 31:19), I will surely have mercy on him, and וְרִחַמְךָ וְהִרְבֶּךָ (Devarim 13:18), and He will have mercy on you and multiply you. In the passive, אֲשֶׁר־בְּךָ יְרֻחַם יָתוֹם (Hoshea 14:4), in You the orphan is shown mercy, and וּמוֹדֶה וְעֹזֵב יְרֻחָם (Mishlei 28:13), one who confesses and forsakes is shown mercy. The adjective is רַחוּם וְחַנּוּן (Tehillim 86:15), merciful and gracious, and with a yud of relation, יְדֵי נָשִׁים רַחֲמָנִיּוֹת (Eichah 4:10), the hands of compassionate women. He says all of them are mercy and the sense is known. On בְּרֹגֶז רַחֵם תִּזְכּוֹר (Chavakuk 3:2) he says רַחֵם may be an infinitive, but it is more correct as a noun.

more.h: Where it is love, not mercy
more.t: אֶרְחָמְךָ (Tehillim 18:2), where the ches carries a kamatz chatuf, he reads as אוֹהַבְךָ, I love You, from the Targum of וַיֶּאֱהַב (Bereishis 25:28), which is וּרְחֵם. Some read רַחֵם תִּזְכּוֹר from this as well: in the time of anger You will remember the love of the fathers. Ibn Ezra reads אֶרְחָמְךָ from the first sense, I will seek mercy from You.

כָל־פֶּטֶר־רֶחֶם (Shemos 13:12), every first issue of the womb, and אֲשֶׁר בְּצֵאתוֹ מֵרֶחֶם אִמּוֹ (Bamidbar 12:12), as he comes out of his mother's womb. It comes with a patach, רַחַם רַחֲמָתַיִם (Shoftim 5:30), and in pause the resh takes a kamatz, כָּל־פֶּטֶר רָחַם (Yechezkel 20:26). In וְרַחְמָה הֲרַת עוֹלָם (Yirmiyahu 20:17) the heh is quiescent where it ought to carry a mappik.

more.h: The sea coming out of a womb
more.t: By way of borrowing, בְּגִיחוֹ מֵרֶחֶם יֵצֵא (Iyov 38:8) is said of the sea: when He brought it forth it was as one coming out of a womb, and when the waters went out and were gathered He hedged them about with the sand, the limit He set for them, that they should not pass it.

He reads it of the day you were born and came out of the womb: the dew that came down that dawn was yours, as a man says that a dew of blessing came down on the day he was born. Ibn Ezra reads it the borrowed way, from the time the dawn rises, that it went out of its place as though it came out of a womb; and then the pasuk says that if you must make war they will come to you as willing rain, like the dew you were used to seeing in your youth when you were a shepherd.

רַחַם רַחֲמָתַיִם לְרֹאשׁ גֶּבֶר (Shoftim 5:30) he takes of the woman herself, a maiden and two maidens, and says they were called so by way of contempt. וְאֶת־הָרָחָמָה (Devarim 14:17) they said is a bird that pities its young greatly.

מלך.sense: To reign; מֶלֶךְ, a king, with מְלוּכָה, מַמְלָכָה and מַלְכוּת for kingship; a second sense of taking counsel; and מֹלֶךְ, the idol served by fire.

more.t: בְּחֶבְרוֹן מָלַךְ שֶׁבַע שָׁנִים (Melachim I 2:11), in Chevron he reigned seven years, and וּמָלַךְ מֶלֶךְ וְהִשְׂכִּיל (Yirmiyahu 23:5), a king shall reign and prosper. Of a woman, וַעֲתַלְיָה מֹלֶכֶת עַל־הָאָרֶץ (Melachim II 11:3), Asalyah was reigning over the land. Where the verb takes an object, הִמְלִיךְ אֶת־שָׁאוּל (Shmuel I 15:35), he made Shaul king; in the passive, אֲשֶׁר הָמְלַךְ עַל מַלְכוּת כַּשְׂדִּים (Daniel 9:1), who was made king over the kingdom of the Kasdim. He says the sense of kingship is known.

וְאֶת־דְּבַר הַמְּלוּכָה לֹא־הִגִּיד לוֹ (Shmuel I 10:16), the matter of the kingship he did not tell him; מַמְלֶכֶת כֹּהֲנִים (Shemos 19:6), a kingdom of kohanim; מַמְלְכוּת עוֹג (Yehoshua 13:12); and without the added mem, מַלְכוּת כַּשְׂדִּים (Daniel 9:1). The plural is אַרְבַּע מַלְכֻיוֹת (Daniel 8:22), four kingdoms, where, tav and heh being alike, the yud that stands for the heh in the plural takes the place of the tav, as in גָּלוּת, exile, and גָּלֻיּוֹת, exiles. Some read לִמְלֶכֶת הַשָּׁמַיִם (Yirmiyahu 7:18) from this, a great star in the heavens. Written with an alef of prolongation, לְעֵת צֵאת הַמְּלָאכִים (Shmuel II 11:1), at the time kings go out.

וַיִּמָּלֵךְ לִבִּי עָלַי (Nechemiah 5:7) means I took counsel, and it is like the Aramaic מִלְכִּי יִשְׁפַּר עֲלָיךְ (Daniel 4:24), let my counsel be pleasing to you, and like the words of Chazal in Berachos, המלך בקונך וצא, take counsel with your Maker and go out. Some read בֶּן־מַלְכֵי־קֶדֶם (Yeshayahu 19:11) from this, the son of counsellors of old.

Rabbi Yonah read הֲתִמְלֹךְ כִּי אַתָּה מְתַחֲרֶה בָאָרֶז (Yirmiyahu 22:15) from counsel, as do you think in your heart to be like and equal to the great king, and read לַמְחוֹת מְלָכִין (Mishlei 31:3) from counsel too. There is no need, he says, to take them out of the sense of kingship: הֲתִמְלֹךְ is do you fancy yourself a king and take pride in vying with the cedar, that is, with one greater than you, and the kingship is not yours that you should be proud over one greater than you.

אֲשֶׁר יִתֵּן מִזַּרְעוֹ לַמֹּלֶךְ (Vayikra 20:2), who gives of his seed to the Molech, and וּלְמֹלֶךְ שִׁקֻּץ בְּנֵי עַמּוֹן (Melachim I 11:7), are the name of an avodah zarah. Its service was that a man handed his son to the priests, and they made two great fires and passed the son on his feet between the two of them. In לֹא־תִתֵּן (Vayikra 18:21), you shall not give, is the handing to the priests, and לְהַעֲבִיר, to pass over, is the passing through the fire.

אדם.sense: To be red, with אָדוֹם and אֲדַמְדָּם for its shades; אֲדָמָה, ground, field or dust; and אָדָם, man, named for the ground he was taken from.

more.t: אָדְמוּ עֶצֶם מִפְּנִינִים (Eichah 4:7), they were ruddier of bone than pearls, and in the passive וְעֹרֹת אֵילִם מְאָדָּמִים (Shemos 25:5), rams' skins dyed red. So אִם־יַאְדִּימוּ כַתּוֹלָע (Yeshayahu 1:18), if they redden like crimson, and אַל־תֵּרֶא יַיִן כִּי יִתְאַדָּם (Mishlei 23:31), do not look at wine when it reddens. The adjectives are דּוֹדִי צַח וְאָדוֹם (Shir HaShirim 5:10), my beloved is white and ruddy, פָרָה אֲדֻמָּה (Bamidbar 19:2), a red cow, and אַדְמוֹנִי עִם־יְפֵה עֵינַיִם (Shmuel I 16:12), ruddy with fair eyes. אֹדֶם פִּטְדָה (Shemos 28:17) is a stone named for being red.

Where the second and third root letters are doubled, אוֹ אֲדַמְדָּם (Vayikra 13:49), he says it holds much of the redness; and Chazal in Sifra said ירקרק ירוק שבירוקים, yerakrak is the greenest of the greens, and אדמדם is אדום שבאדומים, the reddest of the reds. In נֶגַע לָבָן אֲדַמְדָּם (Vayikra 13:42) and לְבָנָה אֲדַמְדֶּמֶת (Vayikra 13:24) it is blended and mixed of two appearances, white and red.

Man is called after the אֲדָמָה, the ground, that he was taken from, and the species is called by his name, אָדָם. אֲדָמָה comes for land, עַל־פְּנֵי הָאֲדָמָה (Bamidbar 12:3), on the face of the earth; for a field, עֹבֵד אַדְמָתוֹ (Mishlei 12:11), one who works his field, and אִם־עָלַי אַדְמָתִי תִזְעָק (Iyov 31:38); and for dust, וַאֲדָמָה עַל־רֹאשׁוֹ (Shmuel I 4:12), earth on his head. Joined to dust it is אַדְמַת־עָפָר (Daniel 12:2), as טִיט הַיָּוֵן (Tehillim 40:3), miry clay.

more.h: One man, all men, and some of them
more.t: אָדָם stands for the individual, אָדָם כִּי־יַקְרִיב מִכֶּם קָרְבָּן (Vayikra 1:2), a man of you who brings an offering; for the whole, מֵאָדָם עַד־בְּהֵמָה (Bereishis 6:7), from man to beast; and for part of the whole, אֶת־הָאָדָם (Yeshayahu 6:12), the men. וְהוּא יִהְיֶה פֶּרֶא אָדָם (Bereishis 16:12) he glosses as a speaking man who is like a wild ass. In גַּם־בְּנֵי אָדָם גַּם־בְּנֵי־אִישׁ (Tehillim 49:3), בְּנֵי אָדָם are the common people and בְּנֵי־אִישׁ the great, as גִּדְעוֹן בֶּן־יוֹאָשׁ אִישׁ יִשְׂרָאֵל (Shoftim 7:14) means the great one of Israel and their head. וּבְיִשְׂרָאֵל וּבָאָדָם (Yirmiyahu 32:20) is the rest of mankind, that is, the nations, and Yonasan renders it בְּנֵי אֱנָשָׁא, the sons of man.

וְנֶפֶשׁ אָדָם מִן־הַנָּשִׁים (Bamidbar 31:35), persons of the women, and כְּתִפְאֶרֶת אָדָם לָשֶׁבֶת בָּיִת (Yeshayahu 44:13) are women alone. His father reads the second so: like the beauty of a woman, and for what? לָשֶׁבֶת בָּיִת, to sit in a house and for nothing else, as he says וְיַנִּיחֻהוּ תַחְתָּיו, and he sets it in its place, מִמְּקוֹמוֹ לֹא יָמִישׁ, from its place it does not stir. הַרְחֵק מְאֹד בֵאָדָם (Yehoshua 3:16) is the name of a city.

רום.sense: To be high, and to raise up; רָם, high; מָרוֹם, a height; תְּרוּמָה, what is set apart; and raising a hand against a king is rebelling.

more.t: יָדֵנוּ רָמָה (Devarim 32:27), our hand is high, and with the middle root letter showing as an alef, וְרָאֲמָה וְיָשְׁבָה תַחְתֶּיהָ (Zechariah 14:10), it shall be lifted up and dwell in its place; רוּמָה עַל־הַשָּׁמַיִם (Tehillim 57:6), be exalted above the heavens. The adjectives are עַל כָּל־גֵּאֶה וָרָם (Yeshayahu 2:12), on all that is proud and high, הֶהָרִים הָרָמִים (Devarim 12:2), the high mountains, and עֵינַיִם רָמוֹת (Mishlei 6:17), haughty eyes; with an alef, רָאמוֹת לֶאֱוִיל חָכְמוֹת (Mishlei 24:7). A height is עָלִיתָ לַמָּרוֹם (Tehillim 68:19), You went up on high, and מְרֹמֵי קָרֶת (Mishlei 9:3), the heights of the city; a raised place is וַתַּעֲשִׂי־לָךְ רָמָה (Yechezkel 16:24).

הֲרִמֹתִי יָדִי (Bereishis 14:22), I have lifted my hand, תָּרִימוּ תְרוּמָה (Bamidbar 15:20), you shall set apart a terumah, and וּכְסִילִים מֵרִים קָלוֹן (Mishlei 3:35), fools raise up shame. וַיָּרֶם יָד בַּמֶּלֶךְ (Melachim I 11:26) is that he rebelled against him, and that is what raising a hand against him is. On אֲשֶׁר הוּנַף וַאֲשֶׁר הוּרָם (Shemos 29:27), what was waved and what was lifted off, he says he has set out the difference between the two under another root.

more.h: Lifting the ash from the mizbeach
more.t: וְהֵרִים אֶת־הַדֶּשֶׁן (Vayikra 6:3), and he shall lift up the ash: Chazal explained that he lifted a panful of the ash every day and set it east of the ramp. But the carrying out, וְהוֹצִיא אֶת־הַדֶּשֶׁן (Vayikra 6:4), was not every day, only when there was much ash on the mizbeach and no room for the arrangement. Though they brought the heap down each day and took it out, the mitzvah was the daily lifting alone and not the clearing of the mizbeach, for on the regalim they did not clear it and left the heap as it stood, since it is an adornment to the mizbeach.

A man's raising and enlarging comes to him neither from the rising of the sun nor from its setting nor from the wilderness of mountains; it does not come from his striving and running here and there, but only from Hashem, as it says כִּי־אֱלֹהִים שֹׁפֵט זֶה יַשְׁפִּיל וְזֶה יָרִים (Tehillim 75:8), for Elokim is the judge, He lowers one and lifts another. Some sefarim read ממדבר, from the wilderness of, with a patach, and then הָרִים would be from הַר; even so the first is correct, and a patach outside a construct has cases like it, מִשְׁפַּט אֶחָד יִהְיֶה לָכֶם (Vayikra 24:22) and וּמִקְסַם חָלָק (Yechezkel 12:24).
