מִבְחַר וְטוֹב־לְבָנוֹן (Yechezkel 31:16), the choicest and best of Levanon, stands as one construct upon another, as אֶת־מִסְפַּר מִפְקַד־הָעָם (Shmuel II 24:9), the number of the mustering of the people, and חַכְמֵי יֹעֲצֵי פַרְעֹה (Yeshayahu 19:11), the wise men of Pharaoh's counsellors.

תלע.sense: A worm, and Israel likened to one in exile; the crimson dye called by its name; and, by a transposition of letters, the great teeth of a lion.

more.t: כִּי תֹאכְלֶנּוּ הַתֹּלָעַת (Devarim 28:39), for the worm will eat it, and וַיָּרֻם תּוֹלָעִים (Shemos 16:20), it bred worms. By way of figure, אַל־תִּירְאִי תּוֹלַעַת יַעֲקֹב (Yeshayahu 41:14), fear not, worm of Yaakov, because they are weak in exile like a worm; and the Midrash he brings says that as the worm's whole strength is in its mouth, so Israel's whole strength is in prayer.

אִם־יַאְדִּימוּ כַתּוֹלָע (Yeshayahu 1:18), though they be red as crimson, and וְתוֹלַעַת שָׁנִי (Shemos 25:4). He has explained elsewhere that שני is the כרמ"ז, the kermes, and it is called by the word for a worm because of how much of the worm is in it. Or תולע is a word for a colour, so that תולעת שני says a red colour, and שְׁנִי הַתּוֹלַעַת (Vayikra 14:6) says red of colour, that is the fine colour, which is the kermes.

Because the colour is well known and finer than the rest, the word תולע is used without שני, and it is as though שני were said: האמונים עֲלֵי תוֹלָע (Eichah 4:5), those brought up on crimson. And אַנְשֵׁי־חַיִל מְתֻלָּעִים (Nachum 2:4) are men of valour clothed in garments of scarlet.

וָאֲשַׁבְּרָה מְתַלְּעוֹת עַוָּל (Iyov 29:17), I broke the fangs of the wrongdoer, which is a transposition of מַלְתְּעוֹת כְּפִירִים (Tehillim 58:7), the fangs of young lions, and they are the thick teeth.

לתע.sense: The great teeth, a lion's fangs; and a verb from it for their being torn out.

more.t: מַלְתְּעוֹת כְּפִירִים (Tehillim 58:7), the fangs of young lions, which are the large teeth. In the passive, וְשִׁנֵּי כְפִירִים נִתָּעוּ (Iyov 4:10), the teeth of the young lions are broken out, where the form by rights is נִלְתָּעוּ; it means the fangs uprooted and falling out, as יְשַׁרֵשׁ is the uprooting of a root.

שׁנב.sense: The אֶשְׁנָב, a window; that one word is the whole of his gloss.

more.t: בְּעַד הָאֶשְׁנָב (Shoftim 5:28), through the window, and בְּעַד אֶשְׁנַבִּי נִשְׁקָפְתִּי (Mishlei 7:6), I looked out through my window. Of both he says only פירושו חלון, its meaning is a window.

נשׁב.sense: Of the wind, to blow; and where the verb takes an object, to drive a thing off, a sense of making it fly away and hover.

more.t: נָשְׁבָה בּוֹ (Yeshayahu 40:7), said of the wind of Hashem that blew upon it. Where the verb takes an object, יַשֵּׁב רוּחוֹ יִזְּלוּ־מָיִם (Tehillim 147:18), He makes His wind blow and the waters flow, and וַיַּשֵּׁב אֹתָם אַבְרָם (Bereishis 15:11), Avram drove them off. He glosses the root ענין ההפרחה והריחוף, a sense of making fly away and hovering.

אבר.sense: Two senses: might and strength, and so the mighty man and the strong horse; and the wing or pinion, with a verb for flying.

more.t: אַבִּירֵי בָשָׁן (Tehillim 22:13), the strong ones of Bashan, אֶשְׁתּוֹלְלוּ אַבִּירֵי לֵב (Tehillim 76:6), the stout hearted were despoiled, and דַּהֲרוֹת אַבִּירָיו (Shoftim 5:22), the galloping of his strong horses. All of these and their like are לשון עוצם וחוזק, a word of might and strength.

לֶחֶם אַבִּירִים אָכַל אִישׁ (Tehillim 78:25), a man ate the bread of the mighty, he takes of the mon that came down to them from heaven, the heavens themselves being the mighty ones, as is said of them חֲזָקִים כִּרְאִי מוּצָק, strong as a molten mirror.

מִי־יִתֶּן־לִּי אֵבֶר כַּיּוֹנָה (Tehillim 55:7), who would give me a wing like a dove's, אֶרֶךְ הָאֵבֶר (Yechezkel 17:3), long of pinion, and בְּאֶבְרָתוֹ יָסֶךְ לָךְ (Tehillim 91:4), under His pinion He shelters you. Their sense and the like of them is כנף, a wing.

הֲמִבִּינָתְךָ יַאֲבֶר־נֵץ (Iyov 39:26), does the hawk fly by your understanding, which he glosses יעוף, it flies; and the sense is given by what stands beside it in the pasuk, יפרוש כנפיו לתימן, he spreads his wings toward the south.

His father takes הָבֵרוּ הַחִצִּים (Yirmiyahu 51:11) from this root, its form by rights הַאֲבֵרוּ, with the alef falling quiet as it does; it says to set a feather on the arrows so as to make them fly straight.

אגף.sense: Bands of troops, named from wings, with the alef added to the word for a wing.

more.t: אַתָּה וְכָל־אֲגַפֶּיךָ (Yechezkel 39:4), you and all your bands, and וְכָל־אֲגַפָּיו אֱזָרֶה לְכָל־רוּחַ (Yechezkel 12:14), all his bands I will scatter to every wind. His father wrote that the alef is added and the word is his wings, that is, his troops, which are like wings; armies have been called wings already, as וְהָיָה מֻטּוֹת כְּנָפָיו (Yeshayahu 8:8), the spreading of his wings. It is close to Aramaic, where wings are called גַּפִּין, and the dagesh there stands for a missing dalet.

מנה.sense: To count, and to be counted; the מָנֶה, a weight of sixty shekels with a known number in it; and to appoint or assign, with מָנָה, a portion.

more.t: מוֹנֶה מִסְפָּר לַכּוֹכָבִים (Tehillim 147:4), counting the number of the stars, and וּמָנִיתִי אֶתְכֶם לַחֶרֶב (Yeshayahu 65:12), I will count you out to the sword. In לִמְנוֹת יָמֵינוּ כֵּן הוֹדַע (Tehillim 90:12), to number our days, he takes the word as an infinitive; Rabbi Yonah wrote that it is a noun.

more.h: The maneh, a weight and a number
more.t: Rabbi Yehudah set הַמָּנֶה יִהְיֶה לָכֶם (Yechezkel 45:12), the maneh shall be yours, under this sense, and Rabbi Yonah disputed him. Granted that a maneh is a weight, as שְׁלֹשֶׁת מָנִים זָהָב (Melachim I 10:17), three maneh of gold, there is still a known number in it: the maneh is sixty shekels and the shekel twenty gerah, and every weight has its known count of how many ounces are in it.

Chazal use מנה sometimes of a weight, the litra, saying מנה דבילה, a maneh of pressed figs, and sometimes of a number, בתולה גובה מאתים ואלמנה מנה (Kesubos, fifth perek, first mishnah), a virgin collects two hundred and a widow a maneh, which is a hundred zuz. It is one thing either way, since a weight is called a maneh only for the known number in it, those places reckoning a litra at twenty zuz.
עֲשֶׂרֶת מֹנִים (Bereishis 31:41), ten times, which he glosses פעמים, times, the word being used because they are a count.

אֲשֶׁר מִנָּה אֶת־מַאֲכַלְכֶם (Daniel 1:10), who appointed your food, וַיְמַן לָהֶם הַמֶּלֶךְ (Daniel 1:5), the king appointed for them, and וְלֵילוֹת עָמָל מִנּוּ־לִי (Iyov 7:3), nights of toil were assigned to me: all of them ענין הזמנה ומתנה, appointing and giving. The noun is a portion, מְנָת־חֶלְקִי וְכוֹסִי (Tehillim 16:5), the portion of my lot and my cup, and וּמִשְׁלוֹחַ מָנוֹת (Esther 9:19), the sending of portions.

more.h: Why the mon is so named
more.t: וַיִּקְרְאוּ בֵית־יִשְׂרָאֵל אֶת־שְׁמוֹ מָן (Shemos 16:31), the house of Israel called its name mon, and וּמַנְךָ לֹא־מָנַעְתָּ מִפִּיהֶם (Nechemiah 9:20), You did not withhold Your mon from their mouth. Since they knew no name for it they called it מַן, that is, a gift and a portion from Hashem.

פקד.sense: To remember and watch over, for good or to visit sin; to be missing; to muster and number; to command; to put in deposit; and to set a man in charge.

more.t: פָּקַד אֶת־שָׂרָה (Bereishis 21:1), He remembered Sarah, פָּקֹד פָּקַדְתִּי אֶתְכֶם (Shemos 3:16), I have surely remembered you, and וְאֶת־אַחֶיךָ תִּפְקֹד לְשָׁלוֹם (Shmuel I 17:18), see to your brothers' welfare. The same word is used of visiting sin, פֹּקֵד עֲוֹן אָבֹת (Shemos 20:5), visiting the sin of fathers, and עַד־פָּקְדִי אֹתוֹ (Yirmiyahu 32:5) he reads as: until I remember him and take My vengeance of him. All of them are ענין זכירה והשגחה, remembering and watching over a thing. וְאֶל־יוֹשְׁבֵי פְּקוֹד (Yirmiyahu 50:21), the dwellers of Pekod, is Bavel, so called because the time came to visit her sin; Yonasan left it untranslated, perhaps holding it the name of a city of Bavel, and so taking פְּקוֹד וְשׁוֹעַ וְקוֹעַ (Yechezkel 23:23) for names of provinces.

וְלֹא־נִפְקַד מִמֶּנּוּ אִישׁ (Bamidbar 31:49), not a man of us is missing, וְלֹא־נִפְקַד לָהֶם מְאוּמָה (Shmuel I 25:7), nothing of theirs was missing, and פֻּקַּדְתִּי יֶתֶר שְׁנוֹתָי (Yeshayahu 38:10), I am deprived of the rest of my years: the sense is חסרון, lack. כִּי יִפָּקֵד מוֹשָׁבֶךָ (Shmuel I 20:18) is because your seat is empty, you not being there, and וְנִפְקַדְתָּ is that his father will remember him when he sees the seat empty of anyone sitting in it.

more.h: Lest the enemy come, or a leaf fail
more.t: On פֶּן יִפְקֹד עָלֶיהָ לַיְלָה וָיוֹם אֶצֳּרֶנָּה (Yeshayahu 27:3), he reads the visiting as an enemy's: lest the enemy remember her and set his face to fight against her, and night and day I guard her. Dunash ben Labrat reads it of lacking, taking it with לרגעים אשקנה, every moment I water it: lest even her leaf be missing, all the more her fruit.

וַיִּפְקֹד שָׁאוּל אֶת־הָעָם (Shmuel I 13:15), Shaul mustered the people, תִּפְקְדוּ אֹתָם לְצִבְאֹתָם (Bamidbar 1:3), you shall number them by their hosts, and אֵלֶּה פְקוּדֵי הַמִּשְׁכָּן (Shemos 38:21), these are the reckonings of the Mishkan: the sense is ענין מספר ומנין, number and count.

הוּא פָקַד עָלַי לִבְנוֹת־לוֹ בַיִת (Ezra 1:2), he commanded me to build Him a house, which he glosses צוה, commanded, as the Targum has it; and so בְּמִפְקַד יְחִזְקִיָּהוּ הַמֶּלֶךְ (Divrei HaYamim II 31:13), by the command of Chizkiyahu the king. In another sense the word is putting a thing in another's keeping: וַיִּקַּח מִיָּדָם וַיִּפְקֹד בַּבָּיִת (Melachim II 5:24), he took from their hand and stored it in the house, הַפִּקָּדוֹן (Vayikra 5:23), the deposit, and וְהָיָה הָאֹכֶל לְפִקָּדוֹן (Bereishis 41:36), the food shall be a store, a sense of גניזה והנחה, putting away and laying up.

וּפָקְדוּ שָׂרֵי צְבָאוֹת (Devarim 20:9), they shall appoint commanders of hosts, and the man so set, פָקִיד עַל־אַנְשֵׁי הַמִּלְחָמָה (Yirmiyahu 52:25), an officer over the men of war: the sense is מנוי וגזברות, appointment and stewardship. Rabbi Yonah put וַיַּפְקֵד אֹתוֹ לְכָל־סֵבֶל בֵּית יוֹסֵף (Melachim I 11:28), he set him over all the burden of the house of Yosef, in the light form; the accurate books have it in the form that takes an object, and the Mesorah counts two such, this and וַיַּפְקֵד עֲלֵיהֶם אֶת־גְּדַלְיָהוּ (Melachim II 25:22), he set Gedaliah over them. In his own view פְּקֻדָּתוֹ יִקַּח אַחֵר (Tehillim 109:8) belongs here: what he is set over, meaning his wife or his property.

קרה.sense: Three senses: to roof a house with beams, and the beam itself; the city, קִרְיָה; and to happen or befall, with מִקְרֶה, a chance happening.

more.t: הֵמָּה קֵרוּהוּ (Nechemiah 3:3), they roofed it, and הַמְקָרֶה בַמַּיִם עֲלִיּוֹתָיו (Tehillim 104:3), who roofs His upper chambers in the waters: the sense is תקון הקורות, setting the beams in place, and covering the house with them. From it קוֹרָה אֶחָת (Melachim II 6:2), one beam, and בְּצֵל קֹרָתִי (Bereishis 19:8), in the shadow of my roof beam.

יִמַּךְ הַמְּקָרֶה (Koheles 10:18), the roofing sinks, is a name for the whole of the roofing, on the pattern of וְלִמְכַסֶּה עָתִיק (Yeshayahu 23:18): the beams go low and lean to fall because of the dripping that keeps at them.

קִרְיַת חָנָה דָוִד (Yeshayahu 29:1), the city where David encamped, may be a construct whose second word is missing, or the tav may stand in place of a heh; and the same word is לְפִי־קָרֶת (Mishlei 8:3), at the mouth of the city, and בְּצֵאתִי שַׁעַר עֲלֵי־קָרֶת (Iyov 29:7), when I went out to the gate by the city. The Targum of עִיר (Bereishis 4:17) is קַרְתָּא. From this he takes the verb וְהִקְרִיתֶם לָכֶם עָרִים (Bamidbar 35:11), you shall set up cities for yourselves.

נִלְכְּדָה קִרְיָתָיִם (Yirmiyahu 48:1), Kiryasayim is taken, may well be a city of Moav, since he lists it among the cities of Moav, וְעַל קִרְיָתַיִם וְעַל־בֵּית גָּמוּל (Yirmiyahu 48:23). So too נִלְכְּדָה הַקְּרִיֹּות (Yirmiyahu 48:41), which is either each one of the cities or the name of a Moavite city, named again in וְעַל־קְרִיֹּות וְעַל־בָּצְרָה (Yirmiyahu 48:24); the definite heh on it does not bar that, as הָעַי (Yehoshua 7:2) and בַּשִּׁטִּים (Bamidbar 25:1).

אֲשֶׁר קָרְךָ בַּדֶּרֶךְ (Devarim 25:18), what befell you on the way, וְקָרָהוּ אָסוֹן (Bereishis 44:29), harm will befall him, and וַיִּקֶר מִקְרֶהָ (Rus 2:3), her chance fell out. כִּי מִקְרֶה בְנֵי־הָאָדָם וּמִקְרֶה הַבְּהֵמָה (Koheles 3:19) he reads as: the sons of man are a happening in the world, and so the beast, and one happening is theirs in their death. וְאִם־תֵּלְכוּ עִמִּי קֶרִי (Vayikra 26:21) is that you say the sufferings He brings on you are a matter of chance and not the requital of your sins.

מצא.sense: To find and to be found; what befalls a man, since it finds him; to be enough; and, where the verb takes an object, to bring a thing to hand.

more.t: מָצָא חֵן בַּמִּדְבָּר (Yirmiyahu 31:2), found favour in the wilderness, וְלֹא־מָצְאָה הַיּוֹנָה מָנוֹחַ (Bereishis 8:9), the dove found no resting place, and כִּי־חַיִּים הֵם לְמֹצְאֵיהֶם (Mishlei 4:22), they are life to those who find them.

אֵין־בְּשׂוֹרָה מֹצֵאת (Shmuel II 18:22), no tidings are found, has the alef quiet, against כְּמוֹצְאֵת שָׁלוֹם (Shir HaShirim 8:10), as one who finds peace, where it keeps its vowel. He reads it: the tidings find you no place now to bring news today, and Yonasan renders וְלָךְ לֵית בְּסוֹרָא מִתְיְהַב, no tidings are given you. At the end of the entry he offers another reading, that the word is מזדמנת, coming to hand: no reward will fall to you by this news.

In אִם אֶת־כָּל־דְּגֵי הַיָּם יֵאָסֵף לָהֶם וּמָצָא לָהֶם (Bamidbar 11:22), he takes the last words as it will be found for them, or else it will suffice them. So too לֹא־יִמָּצֵא לָנוּ הָהָר (Yehoshua 17:16), the hill will not suffice us.

more.h: What his father says of the meat
more.t: His father reads it so: when they craved, they had flocks and herds in plenty, but could not eat of them until they were brought to the door of the Ohel Moed for the sprinkling of the blood and the burning of the fats, and none of a man's household who was tamei could eat. Moshe was saying that were flocks and herds slaughtered for them so that they might slaughter anywhere, it would truly suffice them, and so all the fish of the sea; but with that not so, how were they to eat meat enough? He was answered (Bamidbar 11:23) that Hashem's hand is not short, and that He would give them meat enough besides flocks, herds and fish.

אֵת כָּל־הַתְּלָאָה אֲשֶׁר מְצָאָתַם בַּדֶּרֶךְ (Shemos 18:8), all the hardship that befell them on the way, וּמְצָאֻהוּ רָעוֹת רַבּוֹת (Devarim 31:17), many evils will befall him, and אֵת כָּל־הַמֹּצְאוֹת אוֹתָם (Yehoshua 2:23), which he glosses הקורות המוצאות אותם, the happenings that met them.

וְהִנֵּה אָנֹכִי מַמְצִיא אֶת־הָאָדָם אִישׁ בְּיַד־רֵעֵהוּ (Zechariah 11:6), I am delivering men each into his fellow's hand, and וְאֶת־הָעֹלָה הִמְצִיאוּ אֵלָיו לִנְתָחֶיהָ (Vayikra 9:13), they presented the olah to him in its pieces. All of them are ענין המציאה, finding, which is like הזמנה, a thing brought to hand.

פרח.sense: To blossom, and the blossom; a plague breaking out and spreading on the skin; the young of birds and of men; and to fly.

more.t: פָּרַח מַטֵּה־אַהֲרֹן (Bamidbar 17:23), Aharon's staff blossomed, and צַדִּיק כַּתָּמָר יִפְרָח (Tehillim 92:13), the righteous blossoms like a palm; where the verb takes an object, וְהִפְרַחְתִּי עֵץ יָבֵשׁ (Yechezkel 17:24), I will make a dry tree blossom. Of the sense itself he says only הענין ידוע, it is known.

וַיֹּצֵא פֶרַח וַיָּצֵץ צִיץ (Bamidbar 17:23), it brought forth a פֶּרַח and budded a bud: פֶּרַח here is the leaves coming out first and the bud after, which is the reverse of the almond tree's nature, and it was so to make the miracle greater.

A sense near the first, of a thing showing itself and spreading: וְאִם־פָּרוֹחַ תִּפְרַח הַצָּרַעַת (Vayikra 13:12), if the tzaraas breaks out, בַּשְּׁחִין פָּרָחָה (Vayikra 13:20), it broke out in the boil, and פֹּרֵחַ בָּאָדָם וּבַבְּהֵמָה (Shemos 9:10), breaking out on man and beast.

עַל־יָמִין פִּרְחַח יָקוּמוּ (Iyov 30:12), the young rise at my right: the small ones and the youths, rising at his right to mock him. So too the young of birds are called אפרוחים, as אֶפְרֹחִים אוֹ בֵיצִים (Devarim 22:6), fledglings or eggs, and Chazal say פרחי כהונה, the young sons of the kohanim. Others take פרחח for a compound word whose form is פֶּרַח חָח, the blossom of a thorn, pointing at men who are base and despised, likened to the blossom of thorn and brier, which has nothing of substance in it.

אֶת־הַנְּפָשׁוֹת לְפֹרְחוֹת (Yechezkel 13:20), which he glosses מעופפות, flying; and the Targum of יְעוֹפֵף עַל־הָאָרֶץ (Bereishis 1:20), let it fly over the earth, is יְפָרַח עַל אַרְעָא. The pasuk means hunting the souls to kill them, so that their souls fly off and are gone.

נפל.sense: To fall, in all its uses: falling in war, going over to the enemy, being less than another; and the miscarried child, the refuse of grain, and the giants.

more.t: לֹא־נָפַל דָּבָר אֶחָד (Yehoshua 23:14), not one thing failed, and וְכִי־נָפְלָה אֵימַתְכֶם עָלֵינוּ (Yehoshua 2:9), your dread has fallen upon us. Of going over to another side, לְכוּ וְנִפְּלָה אֶל־מַחֲנֵה אֲרָם (Melachim II 7:4), let us go over to the camp of Aram, and אֶל־הַכַּשְׂדִּים אַתָּה נֹפֵל (Yirmiyahu 37:13), you are going over to the Kasdim. All of them, he says, are one sense, each read by what it stands in.

לֹא־נֹפֵל אָנֹכִי מִכֶּם (Iyov 12:3), I am not less than you, which he glosses פחות, lesser; and וַיִּפְּלוּ מְאֹד בְּעֵינֵיהֶם (Nechemiah 6:16), they were fallen and much lowered in their own eyes against us, since they saw the wall built against their will.

וְנָפַל חָלָל בְּתוֹכְכֶם (Yechezkel 6:7), a slain man falls among you, and with the lamed doubled וְנִפְלַל חָלָל בְּתוֹכָהּ (Yechezkel 28:23), which Yonasan renders כַּד יִתְרְמוּן קְטִילִין בְּגַוָהּ, when the slain are cast down in her midst; or the word is from the root פְּלִילִים and its sense, as Rabbi Yehudah wrote.

עַל־פְּנֵי כָל־אֶחָיו נָפָל (Bereishis 25:18) he takes as his lot falling there, or in the sense of שָׁכֵן, dwelling; and so נֹפְלִים בָּעֵמֶק (Shoftim 7:12), lying in the valley. וְאִם־יִפּוֹל עֵץ (Koheles 11:3), if a tree falls, may be read with them.

וּמַפַּל בַּר (Amos 8:6), the refuse of grain, what falls out of it through the sieve; מַפֶּלֶת הָאַרְיֵה (Shoftim 14:8), the carcass of the lion, the place where it fell; and טוֹב מִמֶּנּוּ הַנָּפֶל (Koheles 6:3), better than he is the stillborn, the child a woman miscarries, so called because it falls dead.

הַנְּפִלִים הָיוּ בָאָרֶץ (Bereishis 6:4), the fallen ones were in the land: men of great stature, called so because a man falls from fear of them, they being so tall, and for that reason they are called האימים, the dread ones, as well. So too הַר־נוֹפֵל יִבּוֹל (Iyov 14:18), which he glosses גבוה ותלול, high and steep.

דרג.sense: He gives no gloss at all; the entry is two pesukim and the Targum that renders going up by steps as בְּדַרְגִּין, by steps.

more.t: בְּסֵתֶר הַמַּדְרֵגָה (Shir HaShirim 2:14), in the covert of the steps, and וְנָפְלוּ הַמַּדְרֵגוֹת (Yechezkel 38:20), the steps will fall. He glosses neither; what he adds is that the Targum of וְלֹא־תַעֲלֶה בְמַעֲלֹת (Shemos 20:23), you shall not go up by steps, is וְלָא תִסַּק בְּדַרְגִּין.

זרח.sense: To shine out, said of the sun; and from it מִזְרָח, the east, and אֶזְרָח, the native, because both are uncovered and seen.

more.t: שֶׁמֶשׁ זָרְחָה וְנוֹדַד (Nachum 3:17), the sun rose and it fled, and הָאֹמֵר לַחֶרֶס וְלֹא יִזְרָח (Iyov 9:6), which he reads of the night, the pasuk going on to seal up the stars by day. The quarter where the sun rises is called מִזְרָח, as מִמִּזְרַח שֶׁמֶשׁ עַד מְבוֹאוֹ (Tehillim 113:3), and the noun is לְנֹגַהּ זַרְחֵךְ (Yeshayahu 60:3).

more.h: Why the tzaraas is said to shine
more.t: וְהַצָּרַעַת זָרְחָה בְמִצְחוֹ (Divrei HaYamim II 26:19) he glosses as its being uncovered, since the rising of the sun is the uncovering of it: until it rises it is hidden, and in rising it is uncovered and seen. Or else, he offers, it says זרחה because the tzaraas was bright as the sun, which is why it is called בַהֶרֶת.

more.h: Why a native is called אזרח
more.t: כְּאֶזְרָח מִכֶּם יִהְיֶה לָכֶם (Vayikra 19:34): he is the settled man, long in the city, because he is uncovered to all and it is known who he is and whose family; but the stranger is covered, and no man knows who he is or whose family. By the same figure כְּאֶזְרָח רַעֲנָן (Tehillim 37:35) is the green and sappy tree, uncovered and seen in its beauty and its freshness.

סוה.sense: The whole entry is one line: the מַסְוֶה of Shemos 34:33 is the veil.

more.t: וַיִּתֵּן עַל פָּנָיו מַסְוֶה (Shemos 34:33), he put a מסוה on his face, which he glosses as הצעיף, the veil, and names in his own vernacular.

סלם.sense: A ladder; of the sense he says only that it is known.

more.t: One line, on וְהִנֵּה סֻלָּם מֻצָּב אַרְצָה (Bereishis 28:12), and behold a ladder set on the ground. Of it he says only ידוע, it is known.

חוט.sense: A thread; of the sense he says only that it is known.

more.t: כְּחוּט הַשָּׁנִי שִׂפְתֹתַיִךְ (Shir HaShirim 4:3), your lips are like a thread of scarlet; and the Targum renders פְּתִיל תְּכֵלֶת (Bamidbar 15:38), a cord of techeiles, as חוּטָא דִתְכֶלְתָּא, a thread of techeiles.

גרל.sense: The lot; of the sense he says only that it is known.

more.t: The pesukim and nothing more: גּוֹרָל אֶחָד, one lot, for Hashem, וְגוֹרָל אֶחָד לַעֲזָאזֵל, and one lot for Azazel, and עַל שְׁנֵי הַשְּׂעִירִם גֹּרָלוֹת, lots on the two goats (Vayikra 16:8); וַיִּפֹּל הַגּוֹרָל עַל יוֹנָה (Yonah 1:7), the lot fell on Yonah; אַתָּה תּוֹמִיךְ גּוֹרָלִי (Tehillim 16:5), You uphold my lot. Of all of them he says only ידוע, their sense is known.

רמך.sense: The mares: בְּנֵי הָרַמָּכִים (Esther 8:10), sons of the mares, as his father takes it, Arabic calling a mare רמכה.

more.t: His father reads בְּנֵי הָרַמָּכִים as בני הסוסיות, sons of the mares, since in Arabic a mare is called רמכה.

אחשרתרנים, the word standing next to it in the pasuk, he takes as a large beast of two kinds, from a horse and from a donkey, אח"ש meaning large in Persian; and perhaps, he says, they were large mules, themselves sons of the mares.

טבר.sense: The navel; and because the navel is the middle of the body, the middle and high point of the earth is called טַבּוּר הָאָרֶץ.

more.t: In Aramaic the word is a known one for the navel, the שורר; and Chazal use it much, as פיו סתום וטבורו פתוח (Niddah 30b), its mouth closed and its navel open.

Since the navel is the middle of the body, a place that is the earth's middle and its height is called by the word: מֵעִם טַבּוּר הָאָרֶץ (Shoftim 9:37), from the middle of the land, and יֹשְׁבֵי עַל טַבּוּר הָאָרֶץ (Yechezkel 38:12), those dwelling on the middle of the earth.

כבל.sense: A fetter, and in the plural chains of iron; the land called אֶרֶץ כָּבוּל is read from a foot held fast in the ground.

more.t: עִנּוּ בַכֶּבֶל (Tehillim 105:18), his foot afflicted with the fetter; and בְּכַבְלֵי בַרְזֶל (Tehillim 149:8), which he glosses שלשלאות של ברזל, chains of iron.

more.h: Why the land is called כָּבוּל
more.t: On אֶרֶץ כָּבוּל (Melachim I 9:13) it is explained that the land is so named because the foot sinks and is held fast in it from all the mud there, or else that it was sand. Chazal say (Shabbos 54a) it is ארץ שאינה עושה פירות, a land that brings out no fruit; Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak says it was a land of חמטון, the foot sinking in it כי כבלא, like a fetter, and חמטון, he says, is sand.

חלשׁ.sense: To be weak and grow faint; and where the verb takes an object, to break and crush.

more.t: וְגֶבֶר יָמוּת וַיֶּחֱלָשׁ (Iyov 14:10), which he reads as: he had already weakened, since a man falls ill before he dies.
וַיַּחֲלשׁ יְהוֹשֻׁעַ (Shemos 17:13), Yehoshua broke them and crushed them; and so חוֹלֵשׁ עַל גּוֹיִם (Yeshayahu 14:12), where עַל stands as though added, the sense holding without it.
הַחַלָּשׁ יֹאמַר גִּבּוֹר אָנִי (Yoel 4:10), let the weak one say I am mighty; and the noun קוֹל עֲנוֹת חֲלוּשָׁה (Shemos 32:18), a sound of crying of weakness.

Chazal take חוֹלֵשׁ עַל גּוֹיִם as casting a lot over them, from מטילין חלשים על הקדשים ביום טוב (Shabbos 148b), that lots are cast over the holy portions on Yom Tov, אבל לא על המנות, but not over the portions; and at Shabbos 149b the Gemara asks what shows that חלשים is the language of a lot, answering from this very pasuk.

שׁקל.sense: To weigh, chiefly the weighing out of silver; the entry is largely the forms, מִשְׁקָל, מִשְׁקוֹל and the rest, and how each is pointed.

more.t: כֶּסֶף יִשְׁקֹל (Shemos 22:16), he shall weigh out silver; וָאֶשְׁקֲלָה לּוֹ אֶת הַכֶּסֶף (Yirmiyahu 32:9), and I weighed him out the silver; in the passive נִשְׁקַל הַכֶּסֶף (Ezra 8:33), the silver was weighed. Of weighing anything else, וְשָׁקַל בַּפֶּלֶס הָרִים (Yeshayahu 40:12), He weighed the mountains in a balance, and וְלֹא יִשָּׁקֵל כֶּסֶף מְחִירָהּ (Iyov 28:15), silver is not weighed out as her price.

וָאֶשְׁקֲלָה לּוֹ (Yirmiyahu 32:9) and וָאֶשְׁקֲלָה עַל יָדָם (Ezra 8:26) both carry a shva and a pasach under the kuf; וָאֶשְׁקֳלָה (Ezra 8:25), and I weighed out to them, carries a kamatz chatuf instead.

מֹאזְנֵי מִשְׁקָל (Yechezkel 5:1), scales for weighing; בֶּקַע מִשְׁקָלוֹ (Bereishis 24:22), a beka in weight; בְּמִשְׁקוֹל עֶשְׂרִים שֶׁקֶל לַיּוֹם (Yechezkel 4:10), at a weight of twenty shekel a day; and two further forms carrying a tav, at Yeshayahu 28:17 and Melachim II 21:13. The שֶׁקֶל itself he brings from בְּשֶׁקֶל הַקֹּדֶשׁ (Shemos 30:13), by the holy shekel, with עֶשְׂרִים גֵּרָה הַשֶּׁקֶל, the shekel is twenty gerah.

רמם.sense: To be high and to rise; and where the verb takes an object, to exalt and magnify. Separately רִמָּה, the worm, and to breed worms.

more.t: רֹאשׁ כּוֹכָבִים כִּי רָמּוּ (Iyov 22:12), the head of the stars, that they are high; וַיָּרָם כְּבוֹד, the glory of Hashem rose from off the keruv (Yechezkel 10:4); וַיֵּרֹמּוּ הַכְּרוּבִים (Yechezkel 10:15), the keruvim were lifted; הֵרֹמּוּ מִתּוֹךְ הָעֵדָה הַזֹּאת (Bamidbar 17:10), be lifted up from among this congregation. רוֹמּוּ מְעַט וְאֵינֶנּוּ (Iyov 24:24) he reads of the wicked: they grew proud and rose a little, and are gone, for in a moment they perish.

וְרוֹמַם תַּחַת לְשׁוֹנִי (Tehillim 66:17), meaning what is under my tongue exalts and magnifies Him, a hint at the heart. יַחַד לֹא יְרוֹמֵם (Hoshea 11:6): together not one of them exalts HaKadosh Baruch Hu or magnifies Him, though the prophets rebuke them and call them to return to the Most High and exalt Him in their prayer; so the rebukes avail nothing.

more.h: The three words take an object
more.t: עַל כֵּן לֹא תְרוֹמֵם (Iyov 17:4) he joins to the pasuk beside it as a prayer: do not exalt one who tells his fellows smooth things and will not rebuke him truly for his sins, for even those among his fellows who know the truth is with him speak smoothly to condemn him unjustly. These three words, he says, take an object, and are not intransitive as Rabbi Yonah holds; and he allows that all three may instead belong to the roots weak in the middle letter.

וְרִמָּה תְּכַסֶּה עֲלֵיהֶם (Iyov 21:26), the worm covers them; תַּחְתֶּיךָ יֻצַּע רִמָּה (Yeshayahu 14:11), the worm is spread beneath you; מְתָקוֹ רִמָּה (Iyov 24:20), the worm finds him sweet. Of these he says only that the sense is known.
וַיָּרֻם תּוֹלָעִים וַיִּבְאַשׁ (Shemos 16:20), it bred worms and stank, pointed with a shuruk to hold it apart from וַיָּרָם כְּבוֹד, the rising of the glory of Hashem (Yechezkel 10:4).

טבח.sense: To slaughter a beast for food; the טַבָּח is the one who does it, and טֶבַח, טִבְחָה and מַטְבֵּחַ are the slaughtering itself.

more.t: וּטְבָחוֹ אוֹ מְכָרוֹ (Shemos 21:37), he slaughtered it or sold it; שׁוֹרְךָ טָבוּחַ לְעֵינֶיךָ (Devarim 28:31), your ox slaughtered before your eyes; וּטְבֹחַ טֶבַח וְהָכֵן (Bereishis 43:16), slaughter and make ready; טָבַחְתָּ לֹא חָמָלְתָּ (Eichah 2:21), You slaughtered and did not pity; כַּשֶּׂה לַטֶּבַח יוּבָל (Yeshayahu 53:7), led like a lamb to the slaughter.

וַיָּרֶם הַטַּבָּח אֶת הַשּׁוֹק (Shmuel I 9:24), the slaughterer lifted the thigh; שַׂר הַטַּבָּחִים (Bereishis 39:1), the chief of the slaughterers; and in the feminine לְרַקָּחוֹת וּלְטַבָּחוֹת (Shmuel I 8:13), as perfumers and as slaughterers. The other noun is הָכִינוּ לְבָנָיו מַטְבֵּחַ (Yeshayahu 14:21), prepare a slaughter for his sons.

Rabbi Yonah divided some of them off to the sense of cooking, and most of the commentators did the same, likening them to Arabic, where one who cooks meat is called by this word, the ches standing for a kaf. In his own view there is no need for that, since every one of them can be explained as slaughtering.

שׁחט.sense: To slaughter; and because slaughtering is a drawing of the knife, the word also describes gold drawn out fine.

more.t: וְשָׁחַט אֶת בֶּן הַבָּקָר (Vayikra 1:5), he shall slaughter the young bull; שׁוֹחֵט הַשּׁוֹר (Yeshayahu 66:3), one who slaughters the ox; in the passive הֲצֹאן וּבָקָר יִשָּׁחֵט לָהֶם (Bamidbar 11:22), shall flocks and herds be slaughtered for them; and the noun שְׁחִיטַת הַפְּסָחִים (Divrei HaYamim II 30:17), the slaughtering of the pesachim.

Rabbi Yonah made וּבְשַׁחֲטָם אֶת בְּנֵיהֶם (Yechezkel 23:39), when they slaughtered their children, belong to the heavy form. It is sounder, he says, as an infinitive of the simple one, like the form at Hoshea 5:2.

Shechitah is done by carrying the knife forward and back, because the word is the language of drawing, as חץ שחוט (Yirmiyahu 9:7), a drawn arrow. Chazal learn from that pasuk (Chullin 30b) that severing the head at a single stroke is invalid, since the knife must be drawn across the neck and carried back and forth; and the Sifra on parshas Tzav says there is no language of shechitah but the language of drawing.

זָהָב שָׁחוּט (Divrei HaYamim II 9:16), drawn gold, so called because fine gold is soft enough from its great worth to be drawn out and spread; and Chazal say (Chullin 30b) זהב השחוט שהיה נמשך כשעוה, the drawn gold that stretched like wax. His father takes חץ שחט as an adjective like שׁוֹחֵט, that is, a killing arrow.

שֹחט.sense: To press or squeeze out; he glosses it ענין עצור, a sense of pressing.

more.t: וָאֶשְׂחַט אֹתָם אֶל כּוֹס פַּרְעֹה (Bereishis 40:11), I pressed them into Pharaoh's cup; and the Mishnah uses the word too (Shabbos 143b), of pressing להוציא מהן משקין, to bring the liquid out of them.

בקע.sense: To split or cleave open; from it בֶּקַע, the half shekel split off from the shekel, and בִּקְעָה, a plain lying level among the mountains.

more.t: בָּקַע יָם וַיַּעֲבִירֵם (Tehillim 78:13), He split the sea and brought them across; יְבַקַּע צֻרִים בַּמִּדְבָּר (Tehillim 78:15), He splits rocks in the wilderness. Of men breaking into a camp or a city, וַיִּבְקְעוּ שְׁלשֶׁת הַגִּבֹּרִים בְּמַחֲנֵה פְלִשְׁתִּים (Shmuel II 23:16), the three mighty men broke through the camp of the Pelishtim, and in the passive הָבְקְעָה הָעִיר (Yirmiyahu 39:2), the city was breached.

נִבְקְעוּ כָּל מַעְיְנוֹת תְּהוֹם רַבָּה (Bereishis 7:11), all the springs of the great deep were split open; כִּי נִבְקְעוּ בַמִּדְבָּר מַיִם (Yeshayahu 35:6), waters broke open in the wilderness; אָז יִבָּקַע כַּשַּׁחַר אוֹרֶךָ (Yeshayahu 58:8), then your light will break open like the dawn.
In וּבָקְעָה וְדָגְרָה בְצִלָּהּ (Yeshayahu 34:15) the splitting is the chick's coming out of the egg, and so בֵּיצֵי צִפְעוֹנִי בִּקֵּעוּ (Yeshayahu 59:5), they split open the adder's eggs.
בֶּקַע לַגֻּלְגֹּלֶת (Shemos 38:26), a beka a head, is half a shekel, and carries the name because it is split off from the shekel.

יֹצְאִים בַּבִּקְעָה וּבָהָר (Devarim 8:7), going out in plain and hill; וְהָרְכָסִים לְבִקְעָה (Yeshayahu 40:4), the ridges made a plain; וַיִּמְצְאוּ בִקְעָה (Bereishis 11:2), they found a plain. It is a level place among the mountains, and he counts these too with the first sense.

פעם.sense: A time, an occurrence; and separately a striking and breaking, from which the bell is named; and the foot, and a corner.

more.t: פַּעַם חוּץ פַּעַם בָּרְחֹבוֹת (Mishlei 7:12), one time outside, one time in the streets; זֹאת הַפַּעַם (Bereishis 2:23), this time; אַךְ הַפַּעַם הַזֶּה (Shoftim 16:28), only this once.

Rabbi Yonah reads לְפַעֲמוֹ (Shoftim 13:25) from that first sense: prophecy began to come to him a first time. Or it is to break and crush him, from וַתִּפָּעֶם רוּחוֹ (Bereishis 41:8), his spirit was troubled, and נִפְעַמְתִּי וְלֹא אֲדַבֵּר (Tehillim 77:5), I am broken and cannot speak, a language of breaking and crushing; and that, he says, is the right one. So too וַתִּתְפָּעֶם רוּחוֹ (Daniel 2:1).

אֶת הוֹלֶם פָּעַם (Yeshayahu 41:7) is the breaking of the blow or the blow that breaks; or פעם is the name of the tool one strikes with, the hammer, as the Targum renders it דִמְטַפַּח בְקוּרְנְסָא, one who strikes with a hammer. From the same the bell is called פעמון, since it rattles and is struck by the clapper inside it: וַיִּתְּנוּ אֶת הַפַּעֲמֹנִים בְּתוֹךְ הָרִמֹּנִים (Shemos 39:25), a bell set between one pomegranate and the next. Chazal read לְפַעֲמוֹ likewise (Sotah 9b), the spirit of prophecy ringing before him like a bell.

מַה יָּפוּ פְעָמַיִךְ (Shir HaShirim 7:2), how beautiful your feet; הָרִימָה פְעָמֶיךָ (Tehillim 74:3), lift up your steps; פַּעֲמֵי דַלִּים (Yeshayahu 26:6), the feet of the poor. Some read הָרִימָה פְעָמֶיךָ instead as מהלמותיך, your blows. From the sense of feet they explain also צֵלָע אֶל צֵלָע שָׁלוֹשׁ וּשְׁלֹשִׁים פְּעָמִים (Yechezkel 41:6), chamber against chamber thirty-three times, which Yonasan rendered thirty-three, eleven to a row.
עַל אַרְבַּע פַּעֲמֹתָיו (Shemos 25:12), which he takes as its four corners.

עקב.sense: The heel, and the tracks a foot leaves; from it the end of a thing, and the reward that comes at a deed's end; and separately deceit.

more.t: עָקֹב הַלֵּב מִכֹּל (Yirmiyahu 17:9), the heart is deceitful above all; כָל אָח עָקוֹב יַעְקֹב (Yirmiyahu 9:3), every brother deals deceitfully; וַיַּעְקְבֵנִי זֶה פַעֲמַיִם (Bereishis 27:36), he has supplanted me these two times; and the noun וְיֵהוּא עָשָׂה בְעָקְבָּה (Melachim II 10:19), Yehu acted with cunning. The sense of them all is deceit and craft. Beside these, וְהָיָה הֶעָקֹב לְמִישׁוֹר (Yeshayahu 40:4), the crooked made level, which is the winding road, hard to climb.

Chazal read עֲקֻבָּה מִדָּם (Hoshea 6:8) from cunning: שהיו עוקבין להרוג נפשות (Makkos 10a), that they lay in wait to kill, that is, acted craftily. In another place they gloss עקבה as מלוכלכת, soiled, the Yerushalmi ruling that what has the עקבה of wine in it is forbidden, and explaining the word as what is soiled, from this very pasuk.

וְיָדוֹ אֹחֶזֶת בַּעֲקֵב עֵשָׂו (Bereishis 25:26), his hand holding Esav's heel; וְאַתָּה תְּשׁוּפֶנּוּ עָקֵב (Bereishis 3:15), you will bruise his heel; הִגְדִּיל עָלַי עָקֵב (Tehillim 41:10), he made his heel great over me, as though I were under his foot; and the verb בַּבֶּטֶן עָקַב (Hoshea 12:4), in the womb he took hold of his heel. In the plural the word is the goings: בְּעִקְבֵי הַצֹּאן (Shir HaShirim 1:8), by the tracks of the flock, and וְעִקְּבוֹתֶיךָ לֹא נֹדָעוּ (Tehillim 77:20), the place of Your goings not known.

Because the heel is the end of the body, the word is used of an end: נָטִיתִי לִבִּי לַעֲשׂוֹת חֻקֶּיךָ לְעוֹלָם עֵקֶב (Tehillim 119:112), to the end of the world; וְאֶצְּרֶנָּה עֵקֶב (Tehillim 119:33), to the end of the world, all the days of my life; וְהוּא יָגֻד עָקֵב (Bereishis 49:19), at the last. So too the verb וְלֹא יְעַקְּבֵם כִּי יִשָּׁמַע קוֹלוֹ (Iyov 37:4), He does not hold them back to the end, but brings the thunder straight after the lightning.

Since the reward is the end of the deed, the word is reward: וְהָיָה עֵקֶב תִּשְׁמְעוּן (Devarim 7:12), in reward for your listening; בְּשָׁמְרָם עֵקֶב רָב (Tehillim 19:12), great reward; יָשׁוּבוּ עַל עֵקֶב בָּשְׁתָּם (Tehillim 70:4), in reward of their shame they will turn back; עֵקֶב אֲשֶׁר שָׁמַע אַבְרָהָם (Bereishis 26:5). In the same way אַחֲרִית, the end, is used for reward (Mishlei 23:18).

עֲוֹן עֲקֵבַי יְסוּבֵּנִי (Tehillim 49:6) his father reads: in the days of punishment the evil reward laid up for my end already surrounds me, so why should I fear, since I am receiving my deeds' reward now; עָוֹן there is the reward of sin, as כִּי לֹא שָׁלֵם עֲוֹן הָאֱמֹרִי (Bereishis 15:16). And וְאֶת עֲקֵבוֹ מִיָּם לָעִיר (Yehoshua 8:13), which others took as its rear, his father takes as its ambush, set to the west of the city, as the Targum renders it.

אוה.sense: To desire and long for; separately נָאוָה, comely and beautiful; and a third sense, a boundary.

more.h: With my soul I desired You
more.t: On נַפְשִׁי אִוִּיתִיךָ בַּלַּיְלָה (Yeshayahu 26:9) Rabbi Yonah says the word stands for אִוָּתְךָ, I desired You. No need, he answers: the sense is with my soul I desired You, the bet unwritten, as אַתָּה יָדְךָ גּוֹיִם הוֹרַשְׁתָּ (Tehillim 44:3), with Your hand You drove out nations. His father explains the pasuk: with my soul I desired You, and while רוּחִי בְקִרְבִּי אֲשַׁחֲרֶךָּ, my spirit is within me I seek You; and it says at night because then the heart is free of the world's business.

more.h: Or the sense leans on the suffix
more.t: Rabbi Yaakov ben Elazar wrote in Sefer HaShalem that the sense attaches to the suffix, the yud of נַפְשִׁי and the yud of רוּחִי: though soul and spirit are named, it is as if he had said I desired You. Many are like it, and so וְצַפַּחַת הַשֶּׁמֶן לֹא חָסֵר (Melachim I 17:16), where the lacking falls on the oil and not on the jar.

אִוָּהּ לְמוֹשָׁב לוֹ (Tehillim 132:13), He desired it for His dwelling; the noun בְּכָל אַוַּת נַפְשְׁךָ (Devarim 12:15), all your soul's desire, and in another form תַּאֲוָה נִהְיָה (Mishlei 13:19), a desire fulfilled; וְלֹא תִתְאַוֶּה בֵּית רֵעֶךָ (Devarim 5:18), you shall not desire your fellow's house, the desiring being in the heart. The sense of all of them is desire and longing.

נָאווּ לְחָיַיִךְ (Shir HaShirim 1:10), your cheeks are comely; מַה נָּאווּ עַל הֶהָרִים רַגְלֵי מְבַשֵּׂר (Yeshayahu 52:7), how beautiful on the mountains are the feet of the herald; לֹא נָאוֶה לִכְסִיל כָּבוֹד (Mishlei 26:1), honour is not fitting for a fool; שְׁחוֹרָה אֲנִי וְנָאוָה (Shir HaShirim 1:5), I am black and comely. In all of them the alef is quiescent, and they are the sense of beauty and comeliness.

Rabbi Yehudah brought הַנָּוָה וְהַמְּעֻנָּגָה (Yirmiyahu 6:2), the comely and delicate one, in with them, perhaps having found it written with an alef, which he says we have not found. Rabbi Yonah wrote it without an alef and faulted Rabbi Yehudah for it; there is nothing to fault, since even unwritten the alef is quiescent after the kamatz. He allows that the whole group may belong to the root נאה, which is how Chazal use it: לולב נאה (Shabbos 133b), a fine lulav, and התנאה לפניו במצות, beautify yourself before Him with mitzvos.

עַד תַּאֲוַת גִּבְעֹת עוֹלָם (Bereishis 49:26), וְהִתְאַוִּיתֶם לָכֶם (Bamidbar 34:10) and תְּתָאוּ לְבֹא (Bamidbar 34:8) are the sense of a boundary: as long as the boundary of the everlasting hills stands, the blessings will be on Yosef's head. תְּתָאוּ ought by rule to be תְּתַאֲווּ, and it is well placed in this root so that it has companions in the sense; or it comes from תָּאָה or תָּוָה, or from the root of וְהִתְוִיתָ תָּו (Yechezkel 9:4), close to a boundary in sense, the alef standing in place of a vav.

זכר.sense: To remember; and separately זָכָר, the male, and a third sense of fragrance, the אַזְכָּרָה burned with the minchah.

more.t: וְלֹא זָכַר שַׂר הַמַּשְׁקִים (Bereishis 40:23), the chief of the cupbearers did not remember; זָכַרְנוּ אֶת הַדָּגָה (Bamidbar 11:5), we remember the fish. On זְכָרָנוּ יְבָרֵךְ (Tehillim 115:12) he reads: Hashem, who has always remembered us in His pity, will bless His people.

כִּי זְכֹר אֲנִי וָאַתָּה (Melachim II 9:25) may be a command, remember when I and you were riding in pairs. Rabbi Yitzchak Giat made it an infinitive bound to the word אֲנִי, and וְשַׁבֵּחַ אֲנִי (Koheles 4:2) and אֲנִי פִּי מֶלֶךְ שְׁמוֹר (Koheles 8:2) with it. He answers that וְשַׁבֵּחַ is an adjective, and that פִּי מֶלֶךְ שְׁמוֹר may be a command: I warn you, keep the king's mouth.

זִכָּרוֹן לִבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל (Shemos 39:7), a remembrance for the children of Israel; אֵין זִכְרוֹן לָרִאשֹׁנִים (Koheles 1:11), there is no remembrance of the former ones; סֵפֶר הַזִּכְרֹנוֹת (Esther 6:1), the book of records; תִּמְחֶה אֶת זֵכֶר עֲמָלֵק (Devarim 25:19), you shall blot out the memory of Amalek. מַזְכֶּרֶת עָוֹן (Bamidbar 5:15) he allows may be a verb rather than a noun: the minchah was making her sin remembered, if she had one.

more.h: Against Rabbi Yonah on two forms
more.t: יַעַן הִזָּכֶרְכֶם בַּכַּף תִּתָּפֵשׂוּ (Yechezkel 21:29) is not a past form, as Rabbi Yonah wrote, but stands alone as the rule is: since you are remembered before Me, full of sin as you are, you will be caught in the palm. So too וְכָל מִקְנְךָ תִּזָּכָר (Shemos 34:19), the cattle spoken of in the feminine and its males set apart from it, for a passive past is never found except standing alone.

זָכָר וּנְקֵבָה בְּרָאָם (Bereishis 5:2), male and female He created them; יֵרָאֶה כָּל זְכוּרְךָ (Shemos 34:23), all your males shall appear. Some read זְכָרָנוּ יְבָרֵךְ (Tehillim 115:12) from here, He will bless our males, and then the house of Israel for the females. That reason he rejects, since בית ישראל, the house of Israel, is a general term taking in males and females alike; in his own view the males are named because they were the ones going up for the festival and coming to the Beis HaMikdash.

זִכְרוֹ כְּיֵין לְבָנוֹן (Hoshea 14:8) and מַזְכִּיר לְבֹנָה (Yeshayahu 66:3) are the sense of smell and of a thing gladly received, and the אַזְכָּרָה burned from the minchah belongs there. Rabbi Yonah kept אַזְכָּרָתָהּ (Vayikra 5:12) away from smell and set it under remembrance; that is not right, since even where the minchah carried no levonah, a small fistful of the flour was burned. Nor was he right that the levonah on the bread was never burned, for it was burned on the coming Shabbos when the bread was removed.

צבע.sense: Dyeing, and so a colour; and from the same root he takes the many-coloured bird of prey, the beast named for its colours, and the finger.

more.t: צֶבַע רִקְמָתַיִם (Shoftim 5:31), dyed embroidery, with a segol under the tzadi, and שְׁלַל צְבָעִים (Shoftim 5:30), a spoil of dyed stuffs. The work itself is known from Chazal (Bava Kamma 9:4): one who gives wool to a dyer to dye red for him, and he dyed it black.

הַעַיִט צָבוּעַ נַֽחֲלָתִי לִי (Yirmiyahu 12:9), my inheritance is to me a bird of prey of many colours, called so because it is of one colour and another, as though it had been dyed. They say it is a bird that all the rest gather round to eat because they hate it. Others read עוף צבוע, a dyed bird, as one rolled in blood, which is why the others gather to it.

הַנִּשְׁקָף עַל־גֵּי הַצְּבֹעִים הַמִּדְבָּֽרָה (Shmuel I 13:18), that looks out over the valley of Tzevoim toward the wilderness. The צבוע is a beast Chazal name (Bava Kamma 16a), where Rabbi Meir says even the צבוע, and they said this צבוע is אפא, which is אפעה, since it is their way to hide the guttural letters. Targum Yonasan renders the valley לְחֵילַת אַפְעַיָא. Bereishis Rabbah says this beast comes from a drop of white and has three hundred and sixty five kinds of colour, the number of the days of the sun.

אֶצְבַּע אֱלֹהִים הִוא (Shemos 8:15), it is the finger of Hashem, and אֶצְבָּעוֹ הַיְמָנִית (Vayikra 14:16), his right finger, belong to this root, the alef being added. The Mishnah uses the letters as a verb (Yoma 2:1): where two were equal, the appointed one says to them הצביעו, hold out your fingers, which the Gemara explains as putting out the fingers to be counted.

עין.sense: The eye, and looking; a look of hatred or of hope, the look or colour a thing has, a spring of water, and the sense of the like of a thing.

more.t: כִּי עַיִן בְּעַיִן יִרְאוּ (Yeshayahu 52:8), they shall see eye to eye, and עֵינַיִם לָהֶם וְלֹא יִרְאֽוּ (Tehillim 115:5), they have eyes and do not see. The word is feminine, עַיִן תִּֽלְעַג לְאָב (Mishlei 30:17), an eye that mocks a father, and עֵינֶיךָ תִרְאֶינָה יְרֽוּשָׁלַם (Yeshayahu 33:20), your eyes shall see Yerushalayim, but its plural comes in the masculine too, עֵינֶיךָ לְנֹכַח יַבִּיטוּ (Mishlei 4:25), your eyes shall look straight before you. In לַמְרוֹת עֵנֵי כְבוֹדֽוֹ (Yeshayahu 3:8) the sense is that they rebel even openly, as the next pasuk says that they told their sin and did not hide it (Yeshayahu 3:9), having no shame that would make them hide it; the form עני lacks the yod, which is the root's middle letter.

more.h: Setting the eye on a man
more.t: וַיְהִי שָׁאוּל עוֵֹן (Shmuel I 18:9), Shaul set his eye on David and looked at him with the look of hatred. He holds that a look of hope is said the same way: כָּֽל־ מַעְיָנַי בָּֽךְ (Tehillim 87:7), all my looking and my hope is in You. Chazal used the doubled form of it much (Bava Basra 115a and 89a). שִׁבְעָה עֵינָיִם (Zecharyah 3:9), seven eyes, he reads by the later pasuk (Zecharyah 4:10), where these seven are Hashem's eyes ranging over all the earth: they guard the building so that Israel's adversaries cannot stop the work, and seven stands for many guardings, as שבע יפול צדיק וקם, seven times the righteous falls and rises. And וְהָיִיתָ לָּנוּ לְעֵינָֽיִם (Bamidbar 10:31), you shall be to us for eyes, is that he will show them the good road as the eyes show a man his way, or that they will always have him in sight and be able to repay him good.

וְעֵינוֹ כְּעֵין הַבְּדֹֽלַח (Bamidbar 11:7), its look was as the look of bdolach, and כְּעֵין תַּרְשִׁישׁ (Yechezkel 1:16), in its look. So of a mark on the skin: וְאִם־ בְּעֵינָיו עָמַד הַנֶּתֶק (Vayikra 13:37), if the netek stayed in the look it had, and לֹֽא־הָפַךְ הַנֶּגַע אֶת־ עֵינוֹ (Vayikra 13:55), the mark did not change the look it had at first. Of wine, כִּֽי־ יִתֵּן בַּכֹּיס (Mishlei 23:31), when it gives in the cup, its eye is its colour and its shine. Some take יָצָא מֵחֵלֶב עֵינֵמוֹ (Tehillim 73:7) here too, that their look shines out from their fat, reading יָצָא as shone, like הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ יָצָא עַל־הָאָרֶץ (Bereishis 19:23), the sun had gone out over the earth.

עַל־עֵין הַמַּיִם (Bereishis 16:7), by the spring of water, and it is feminine, עַל־כֵּן קָרָא שְׁמָהּ עֵין הַקּוֹרֵא (Shoftim 15:19), therefore its name was called Ein HaKorei. The plural is עֲיָנֹת וּתְהֹמֹת (Devarim 8:7), springs and deeps, and with an added mem, מַעְיָן נִרְפָּשׂ (Mishlei 25:27), a muddied spring, and מִמַּֽעַיְנֵי הַיְשׁוּעָֽה (Yeshayahu 12:3), from the wells of salvation. עֵין יַֽעֲקֹב (Devarim 33:28), the fountain of Yaakov, is in the manner of מִמְּקוֹר יִשְׂרָאֵֽל (Tehillim 68:27), from the fountain of Israel. Rabbi Yonah counted כָּֽל־ מַעְיָנַי בָּֽךְ (Tehillim 87:7) among these, and it may also be read as all my looking and my watching is in You.

more.h: Of the like of a thing
more.t: Chazal say מעין שמנה עשרה (Berachos, chapter four), something of the like of the eighteen blessings, and מעין כל ברכה, of the like of every blessing, which he glosses מענין כל ברכה, of the matter of every blessing. From this Onkelos renders עֵין יַֽעֲקֹב (Devarim 33:28) as כְּעֵין בִּרְכְּתָא דִבָרֵכִנּוּן, after the manner of the blessing with which he blessed them: as he blessed them, so their lot fell in the land, and each dwelt secure in his portion.

הִנֵּה הוּא־לָךְ כְּסוּת עֵינַיִם (Bereishis 20:16), which he reads as the thousand of silver given to her brother so that he buy her a fine garment worked עינים עינים, in eye figures, as Bereishis Rabbah explains it. And on בְּעֵינִי (Shmuel II 16:12), in my eye, some say the yod that stands between the ayin and the nun belongs after them, and the word is properly בְּעָנְיִי, in my affliction; Yonasan renders it דִמְעַת עֵינִי, the tear of my eye; and it may be read as the matter I am in now.

קשׁה.sense: To be hard or severe, and to make hard: a hard master, a stiff neck, a hardened heart, a hard birth; and the מִקְשָׁה, hammered work, of the Menorah.

more.t: לֹֽא־ יִקְשֶׁה בְעֵינֶךָ (Devarim 15:18), let it not be hard in your eyes, and וַיִּקֶשׁ דְּבַר־אִישׁ יְהוּדָה (Shmuel II 19:44), the word of the men of Yehudah was the harder. The adjective is אֲדֹנִים קָשֶׁה (Yeshayahu 19:4), a hard master; the noun, אֶל־ קְשִׁי הָעָם הַזֶּה (Devarim 9:27), the hardness of this people, with a sheva alone; and in the passive, וְעָבַר בָּהּ נִקְשֶׁה וְרָעֵב (Yeshayahu 8:21), one hardened and hungry passes through it.

כִּי עַם־ קְשֵׁה ־עֹרֶף אָֽתָּה (Devarim 9:6), for you are a people stiff of neck, and וְאֶֽת־עָרְפְּךָ הַקָּשֶׁה (Devarim 31:26), your stiff neck; the phrase means they do not turn to the one who calls them. Its build is like נֹבֶלֶת עָלֶהָ (Yeshayahu 1:30), whose leaf withers, and קְרוּעֵי בְגָדִים (Yeshayahu 36:22), with garments rent.

כִּֽי־ הִקְשָׁה פַרְעֹה לְשַׁלְּחֵנוּ (Shemos 13:15), Pharaoh hardened himself against letting us go, which he explains as hardening his heart, and so מי הִקְשָׁה אליו (Iyov 9:4), whoever hardened his heart against Him; וַיֶּקֶשׁ אֶת־עָרְפּוֹ (Divrei HaYamim II 36:13), he stiffened his neck; וּמַקְשֶׁה לִבּוֹ (Mishlei 28:14), one who hardens his heart.

וַיְהִי בְהַקְשֹׁתָהּ בְּלִדְתָּהּ (Bereishis 35:17), when her labour was hard, which he explains as her making the birth hard upon herself, and וַתְּקַשׁ בְּלִדְתָּֽהּ (Bereishis 35:16), which takes an object in that same sense.

מִקְשָׁה תַּֽעֲשֶׂה אֹתָם (Shemos 25:18), of the keruvim, מִקְשָׁה תֵּֽיעָשֶׂה הַמְּנוֹרָה (Shemos 25:31), of the Menorah, and the idols of Yirmiyahu 10:5 all carry one sense. In וְתַחַת מַֽעֲשֶׂה מִקְשֶׁה (Yeshayahu 3:24) he reads מעשה as standing on its own and not in construct, since it is pointed with a segol, and takes the two words as the trimming and evening of the hair, which was fine and even, and in whose place comes baldness; or else מקשה is said of the מעשה, the evenly ordered hair. Rashi explained the two pesukim of the Mishkan from דָּא לְדָא נָֽקְשָֽׁן (Daniel 5:6), the one knocking against the other, a matter of striking: the smith struck with a hammer and drew the stems and branches out this way and that, all of one body, the stems and knobs not made apart and joined on after.

קשֹה.sense: He gives no sense here. The entry sets out the forms of the word, and says he has explained these vessels at two other roots.

more.t: וּקְשׂוֹתָיו וּמְנַקִיֹתָיו (Shemos 25:29) and וְאֵת קְשׂוֹת הַנָּסֶךְ (Bamidbar 4:7), the vessels of the pouring, with the root's last letter showing in וְאֶת־ הַקְּשָׂוֹת אֲשֶׁר יֻסַּךְ בָּהֵן (Shemos 37:16), the vessels with which it is poured; a form like יֹשְבֵי קְצָוֹת (Tehillim 65:9), those who dwell at the ends.

קשׁח.sense: To be cruel and hard of heart: dealing hardly with one's young, and a heart hardened away from the fear of Hashem.

more.t: הִקְשִׁיחַ בָּנֶיהָ לְּלֹא־לָהּ (Iyov 39:16), she deals hardly with her young as though they were not hers, and תַּקְשִׁיחַ לִבֵּנוּ מִיִּרְאָתֶךָ (Yeshayahu 63:17), You harden our heart away from fearing You: the sense is cruelty and hardness of heart.

On the pasuk in Yeshayahu: seeing the ease of the wicked, the length of our exile and our being trampled by them, our heart hardens over it, as though You were the one making us stray from Your ways and hardening our heart away from Your fear, because their ease is long and ours is exile and trouble.

נגב.sense: The south; and dryness, a parched land, so that the Negev may be the wilderness and its drought or the south, which is named for its heat and waste.

more.t: מֶֽלֶךְ־ הַנֶּגֶב (Daniel 11:5), the king of the south, with six points, and צָפֹנָה וָנֶגְבָּה (Bereishis 13:14), northward and southward: it is the south.

אֶרֶץ הַנֶּגֶב נְתַתָּנִי, you have given me a southern land, which he explains as a waste and parched land; and so כַּֽאֲפִיקִים בַּנֶּֽגֶב (Tehillim 126:4), like streams in the Negev, כְּסוּפוֹת בַּנֶּגֶב (Yeshayahu 21:1), like whirlwinds in the Negev, and מַשָּׂא בַּֽהֲמוֹת נֶגֶב (Yeshayahu 30:6), the burden of the beasts of the Negev.

more.h: Drying, in Targum and in Chazal
more.t: חָֽרְבוּ פְּנֵי הָֽאֲדָמָֽה (Bereishis 8:13), the face of the ground was dry, which the Targum renders נְגוּבוּ אַפֵּי אַרְעָא; and Chazal (Taharos 10:8) say מנגבן והן טהורין, he wipes them dry and they are clean. They use the word much besides.

וְדָוִד קָם מֵאֵצֶל הַנֶּגֶב (Shmuel I 20:41), David rose from beside the Negev, נֶגֶב יְהוּדָה (Shmuel I 27:10), the Negev of Yehudah, אֶל־ נֶגֶב וְאֶל־צִקְלַג (Shmuel I 30:1), to the Negev and to Tziklag, and עָרֵי הַנֶּגֶב סֻגְּרוּ (Yirmiyahu 13:19), the cities of the Negev are shut up: all of them may be the wilderness and the place of drought and dryness, or the south. Or they are level ground, the wilderness being level too; and the south itself is called נֶגֶב, the Negev, because that quarter has much drought and no settlement as the others have, for its heat.

יבשׁ.sense: To be dry and to dry a thing up, and the dry land; and in the same letters a second sense, to be shamed, with pesukim in Yoel he allows either way.

more.t: כִּי יָֽבְשׁוּ אֲפִיקֵי מָיִם (Yoel 1:20), the water channels are dried up; יָֽבְשׁוּ עַצְמוֹתֵינוּ (Yechezkel 37:11), our bones are dried; יָֽבְשָׁה הָאָֽרֶץ (Bereishis 8:14), the earth was dry; וַיִּיבַשׁ הַנָּחַל (Melachim I 17:7), the brook dried up. The sense, he says, is dryness.

On הֵן יַעְצֹר בַּמַּיִם וְיִבָשׁוּ (Iyov 12:15), He holds back the waters and they dry up, Rabbi Yonah wrote that the vav takes a chirik and the yod is quiescent. He says he did not find it so in the accurate books, but with a sheva under the vav and a chirik under the yod.

אֲשֶׁר־ הוֹבִישׁ (Yehoshua 2:10), how He dried up the waters of Yam Suf; הוֹבַשׁתִּי עֵץ לָח (Yechezkel 17:24), I dried up the green tree; וְהֹבִישׁוּ כֹּל מְצוּלוֹת יְאֹר (Zecharyah 10:11), and all the depths of the river shall be dried. Rabbi Yonah set that last as a word standing alone, and he says there is no need: in that pasuk a wind of trouble passes in the sea and strikes up its waves, and the winds dry all the depths of the river. So too תְּיַבֶּשׁ ־גָּֽרֶם (Mishlei 17:22), it dries the bone, and גּוֹעֵר בַּיָּם וַיַּבְּשֵׁהוּ (Nachum 1:4), He rebukes the sea and dries it, where he holds the written yod is the prefix and the root's own yod has dropped, leaving its vowel behind; Rabbi Yehudah said the reverse, and some, his father among them, read it as a form that takes an object outright.

וְנוֹזְלִים עַל־ יַבָּשָׁה (Yeshayahu 44:3), streams on the dry ground, and וְתֵֽרָאֶה הַיַּבָּשָׁה (Bereishis 1:9), let the dry land appear, which may be a noun or an adjective; with a tav for the heh, וְיַבֶּשֶׁת יָדָיו יָצָֽרוּ (Tehillim 95:5), His hands formed the dry land. In another pattern the adjective: עֵץ יָבֵשׁ (Yechezkel 17:24), a dry tree, and נַפְשֵׁנוּ יְבֵשָׁה (Bamidbar 11:6), our soul is dried up.

לֹֽא־עַתָּה יֵבוֹשׁ יַֽעֲקֹב (Yeshayahu 29:22), Yaakov shall not now be shamed; גַּם־ בּוֹשׁ לֹֽא־ יֵבוֹשׁוּ (Yirmiyahu 6:15), they are not ashamed at all; יֵבשׁוּ רֹֽדְפַי (Yirmiyahu 17:18), let my pursuers be shamed; and where it takes an object, הֹבַשְׁתָּ הַיּוֹם אֶת־פְּנֵי כָל־עֲבָדֶיךָ (Shmuel II 19:6), today you have shamed the face of all your servants.

הַגֶּפֶן הוֹבִישָׁה (Yoel 1:12), the vine is shamed, and הוֹבִישׁ תִּירוֹשׁ (Yoel 1:10), the new wine is shamed, he takes by way of figure, as though the vine had shame when it does not give its fruit as it should, like הֹבִישׁוּ אִכָּרִים (Yoel 1:11), the farmers are shamed, and הֹבִישׁוּ חֲכָמִים (Yirmiyahu 8:9), the wise are shamed. But those two may be read instead as a sense of drying and ceasing.

נעם.sense: To be pleasant or lovely: words that please, ways of pleasantness, the sweet singer of Israel. The sense, he says, is known, and belongs to beauty.

more.t: נָעַמְתָּ לִּי מְאֹד (Shmuel II 1:26), you were very pleasant to me; וְשָׁמְעוּ אֲמָרַי כִּי נָעֵֽמוּ (Tehillim 141:6), they shall hear my words, for they are pleasant; וְדַעַת לְֽנַפְשְׁךָ יִנְעָֽם (Mishlei 2:10), knowledge shall be pleasant to your soul.

נְעִמוֹת בִּימִינְךָ נֶֽצַח (Tehillim 16:11), pleasures at Your right hand for ever; כָּל־הוֹן יָקָר וְנָעִֽים (Mishlei 24:4), all precious and pleasant wealth; וּנְעִים זְמִרוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵֽל (Shmuel II 23:1), the sweet singer of Israel; הַנֶּאֱהָבִים וְהַנְּעִימִם (Shmuel II 1:23), the beloved and the pleasant; נִטְעֵי נַֽעֲמָנִים (Yeshayahu 17:10), plantings of pleasantness; דְּרָכֶיהָ דַרְכֵי־ נֹעַם (Mishlei 3:16), her ways are ways of pleasantness; and וּבַל־אֶלְחַם בְּמַנְעַמֵּיהֶֽם (Tehillim 141:4), let me not eat of their dainties.

כִּֽי־ נָעִים כִּֽי־תִשְׁמְרֵם בְּבִטְנֶךָ (Mishlei 22:18) may instead be read from נָע וָנָד (Bereishis 4:12), wandering and moving: if you do not keep them in your belly they will soon be on the move and gone.

מתק.sense: To be sweet and to make sweet: sweetness of speech, sweeter than honey, the sleep of a labourer, and by a borrowing sweet light and sweet counsel.

more.t: מָֽתְקוּ ־לוֹ רִגְבֵי נָחַל (Iyov 21:33), the clods of the valley are sweet to him, and מְתָקוֹ רִמָּה (Iyov 24:20), which he reads either as the worm being sweet to him or as the worm's mouth being sweetened from him.

אִם־ תַּמְתִּיק בְּפִיו רָעָה (Iyov 20:12), though evil be sweet in his mouth, which he calls a borrowed use and takes without an object; and אֲשֶׁר יַחְדָּו נַמְתִּיק סוֹד (Tehillim 55:15), with whom we sweetened counsel together, where it takes one.

וּמֶתֶק שְׂפָתַיִם יֹסִיף לֶֽקַח (Mishlei 16:21), sweetness of lips adds learning; הֶֽחֳדַלְתִּי אֶת־ מָתְקִי (Shoftim 9:11), shall I leave my sweetness; חִכּוֹ מַֽמְתַּקִּים (Shir HaShirim 5:16), his palate is sweetness; מַה־ מָּתוֹק מִדְּבַשׁ (Shoftim 14:18), what is sweeter than honey; וַתְּהִי בְפִי כִּדְבַשׁ לְמָתֽוֹק (Yechezkel 3:3), which he explains as being sweet in his mouth as honey is sweet to a man; מְתוּקָה שְׁנַת הָֽעֹבֵד (Koheles 5:11), sweet is the sleep of the labourer; and by a borrowing, וּמָתוֹק הָאוֹר (Koheles 11:7), and the light is sweet.

סבא.sense: To drink deep and be drunk; from it wine itself is named, and the man who sells it; and by the same letters a nation of the sons of Kush.

more.t: וְנִסְבְּאָה שֵׁכָר (Yeshayahu 56:12), let us fill ourselves with strong drink; זוֹלֵל וְסֹבֵֽא (Devarim 21:20), a glutton and a drunkard; אַל־תְּהִי בְסֹֽבְאֵי ־יָיִן (Mishlei 23:20), be not among the drinkers of wine; וּכְסָבְאָם סְבוּאִים (Nachum 1:10), and drunken as with their drink. סָבָאִים מִמִּדְבָּר (Yechezkel 23:42) he takes as men who have drunk and are drunk.

The wine itself is named from it: סָבְאֵךְ מָהוּל בַּמָּֽיִם (Yeshayahu 1:22), your wine is mixed with water. And so the wine-seller was called סובא, a drinker, as the poet has it, and as Chazal (Avodah Zarah 70b) speak of a woman who sells wine, מסוביתא, the wine-woman, who handed over her key.

כּוּשׁ וּסְבָאִים אַנְשֵׁי מִדָּה (Yeshayahu 45:14), Kush and the Sevaim, men of stature, where it is the name of a nation of the sons of Kush; and מֽוּבָאִים סָבָאִים מִמִּדְבָּר may be read that way as well.

זלל.sense: A glutton, one who eats much meat, set beside the drunkard; and in a second sense, lightness and contempt.

more.t: זוֹלֵל וְסֹבֵֽא (Devarim 21:20), a glutton and a drunkard, and בְּזֹֽלְלֵי בָשָׂר לָֽמוֹ (Mishlei 23:20), among those who gorge on meat: one who eats much meat is called זולל, a glutton, as one who drinks much wine is called סובא, a drunkard.

וְאִם־תּוֹצִיא יָקָר מִזּוֹלֵל (Yirmiyahu 15:19), if you bring out the precious from the vile, and כִּי הָיִיתִי זוֹלֵלָֽה (Eichah 1:11), for I have become despised. The noun is כְּרֻם זֻלֻּת לִבְנֵי אָדָֽם (Tehillim 12:9), which he reads as: when the wicked are lifted high, there is contempt for the sons of men. Rabbi Yonah put הָרִים נָזֹֽלּוּ (Yeshayahu 64:2), the mountains flowed down, under this root, and he holds the right view is that it belongs to נזל, flowing.

איב.sense: To be an enemy; its sense, he says, is hatred.

more.t: One line: וְאָֽיַבְתִּי אֶת־אֹיְבֶיךָ (Shemos 23:22), I will be an enemy to your enemies, and the noun וְאֵיבָה אָשִׁית (Bereishis 3:15), I will put enmity; the sense is hatred.

צרר.sense: To harass and be an enemy, and the straits that come of it; and a second sense, to bind up: a bundle of silver, and צְרוֹר, a pebble.

more.t: וְצָֽרְרוּ אֶתְכֶם (Bamidbar 33:55), they shall harass you; צָרוֹר אֶת־הַמִּדְיָנִים (Bamidbar 25:17), harass the Midianites; כי צֹֽרֲרִים הֵם לָכֶם (Bamidbar 25:18), for they harass you; and וְצַרְתִּי אֶת־ צֹֽרְרֶֽיךָ (Shemos 23:22), I will harass those who harass you. It may be that וִֽיהוּדָה לֹֽא־ יָצֹר אֶת־אֶפְרָֽיִם (Yeshayahu 11:13), Yehudah shall not harass Efraim, is from this root.

מִן־ הַמֵּצַֽר (Tehillim 118:5), out of the strait, and בֵּין הַמְּצָרִֽים (Eichah 1:3), between the straits. Rabbi Yehudah put וְהֵצַר לְךָ (Devarim 28:52), it shall press you, and וַֽהֲצֵרֹתִי לָֽאָדָם (Tzefaniah 1:17), I will press men hard, under this root; he says he has written them at צוּר, along with צַר וְאוֹיֵב (Esther 7:6), an adversary and an enemy, and צַר ־לִי מְאֹד (Shmuel II 24:14), I am in great straits, and it may be that the root of them all is צָרַר.

Rabbi Yehudah set in another sense וְכִֽעֲסַתָּה צָֽרָתָהּ (Shmuel I 1:6), her rival vexed her, and לִצְרֹר לְגַלּוֹת עֶרְוָתָהּ (Vayikra 18:18), to take a rival and uncover her nakedness; he says he has explained the rival at צוּר.

מִי צָֽרַר ־מַיִם בַּשִּׂמְלָה (Mishlei 30:4), who has bound up water in a garment; צֹֽרֵר ־מַיִם בְּעָבָיו (Iyov 26:8), He binds up water in His clouds; כִּצְרוֹר אֶבֶן בְּמַרְגֵּמָה (Mishlei 26:8), as one binds a stone in a sling; and in the passive, וּמְבֻקָּעִים וּמְצֹֽרָרִֽים (Yehoshua 9:4), split and bound up. The noun is צְֽרוֹר ־הַכֶּסֶף לָקַח בְּיָדוֹ (Mishlei 7:20), he took the bundle of silver in his hand, and צְרוֹר הַמֹּר דּוֹדִי לִי (Shir HaShirim 1:13), my beloved is a bundle of myrrh to me: their sense is binding.

וַתִּֽהְיֶינָה צְרֻרוֹת (Shmuel II 20:3), they were shut up till the day of their death, which he holds belongs to binding: as though they were bound and not loosed to marry a man. And וְלֹֽא־יִפּוֹל צְרוֹר אָֽרֶץ (Amos 9:9), not a pebble shall fall to the ground, and אֲשֶֽׁר־לֹֽא־נִמְצָא שָׁם גַּם־ צְרֽוֹר (Shmuel II 17:13), where not even a pebble was found, he explains as a stone, and it is like צוּר, a rock, the two being one sense.

מיר.sense: To exchange one thing for another, and the תמורה, what is given in its place; on one pasuk he adds a second sense, of magnifying.

more.t: הֵמִיר כְּבוֹדוֹ (Yirmiyahu 2:11), he exchanged his glory; וְלֹֽא־ יָמִיר אֹתוֹ (Vayikra 27:10), he shall not exchange it; וְלֹא יָמֵר (Yechezkel 48:14), he shall not exchange, said of the first of the land; and the noun, וְהָֽיָה־הוּא וּתְמֽוּרָתוֹ (Vayikra 27:10), it and what is exchanged for it. Their sense is the exchanging of one thing for another.

הַֽהֵימִיר גּוֹי אֱלֹהִים (Yirmiyahu 2:11), has a nation exchanged its gods: the yod written between the heh and the first root letter is the quiescent letter of הֵקִים, he raised up, and הֵשִׁיב, he brought back, and here it is written against the usual way. He suggests the word is built to carry two senses at once. One is exchange, that a nation has changed its gods for other gods although they are no gods. The other is from וּבִכְבוֹדָם תִּתְיַמָּֽרוּ (Yeshayahu 61:6), and in their glory you shall vaunt yourselves, so that הֵימִיר follows the pattern of הֵיטִיב, he did good, and the sense is: has a nation magnified other gods that are not its own, when neither of them is a god.

חלף.sense: To pass by and be gone; to change a thing or renew it, and changes of garments; and a sense of cutting through, so that knives are called מַֽחֲלָפִים, cutters.

more.t: חָלַף הָלַךְ לֽוֹ (Shir HaShirim 2:11), it has passed and gone; וְחָֽלַפְתָּ מִשָּׁם וָהָלְאָה (Shmuel I 10:3), you shall pass on from there; וְיַֽחֲלֹף וְֽלֹא־אָבִין לֽוֹ (Iyov 9:11), He passes by and I do not perceive Him; כְּסוּפוֹת בַּנֶּגֶב לַֽחֲלֹף (Yeshayahu 21:1), like whirlwinds in the Negev sweeping through; חָלְפוּ חֹק (Yeshayahu 24:5), they passed over the statute. All of them, he says, are a sense of passing.

וְהַֽחֲלִיפוּ שִׂמְלֹֽתֵיכֶֽם (Bereishis 35:2), change your garments; וַתַּֽחֲלֵף אֶת־מַשְׂכֻּרְתִּי (Bereishis 31:41), you changed my wages; כַּלְּבוּשׁ תַּֽחֲלִיפֵם וְֽיַֽחֲלֹֽפוּ (Tehillim 102:27), You change them like a garment and they pass away; אִֽם־יִכָּרֵת וְעוֹד יַֽחֲלִיף (Iyov 14:7), though it be cut down it will yet renew, meaning it will renew its shoots; וְקַשְׁתִּי בְּיָדִי תַֽחֲלִֽיף (Iyov 29:20), my bow renews in my hand, which he explains as my strength and my might renewing my honour for me; and יַֽחֲלִיפוּ כֹחַ (Yeshayahu 40:31), they shall renew strength.

more.h: A change of garments, and in place of
more.t: וַיְגַלַּח וַיְחַלֵּף שִׂמְלֹתָיו (Bereishis 41:14), he shaved and changed his garments; חֲלִפוֹת שְׂמָלֹת (Bereishis 45:22), changes of raiment; וּשְׁלשִׁים חֲלִפֹת בְּגָדִֽים (Shoftim 14:12), thirty changes of garments: all in the sense of renewal and exchange. One thing coming in another's place is עֲשֶׂרֶת אֲלָפִים בַּחֹדֶשׁ חֲלִיפוֹת (Melachim I 5:28), ten thousand a month by courses, these going and those coming. And חֵלֶף עֲבֹֽדַתְכֶם (Bamidbar 18:31), in return for your service, with six points, is what the Targum gives for תַּחַת (Bereishis 4:25), in place of.

אִם־ יַֽחֲלֹף וְיַסְגִּיר (Iyov 11:10), if He cut through and shut up; וְהָאֱלִילִים כָּלִיל יַֽחֲלֹֽף (Yeshayahu 2:18), the idols shall wholly pass away; תַּחְלְפֵהוּ קֶשֶׁת נְחוּשָֽׁה (Iyov 20:24), a bow of brass shall strike him through; and the nouns עַד־בּוֹא חֲלִיפָתִֽי (Iyov 14:14), until my change come, אֲשֶׁר אֵין חֲלִיפוֹת לָמוֹ (Tehillim 55:20), who have no changes, and כָּל־בְּנֵי חֲלֽוֹף (Mishlei 31:8), all the sons of passing. All of these are a sense of cutting off, and the people of the world are called בני חלוף, sons of passing, because death and cutting off from the world come upon them.

His father explains כֶּחָצִיר יַֽחֲלֹֽף (Tehillim 90:5), like grass that passes, from this: if they are there at night they are not there in the morning, for the grass is cut off, the word standing alone in that sense. And if בַּבֹּקֶר יָצִיץ וְחָלָף (Tehillim 90:6), in the morning it blossoms and is renewed, is like וְעוֹד יַֽחֲלִיף (Iyov 14:7), it will yet renew, then by evening it is cut down and dried.

Knives are called מחלפים, מַֽחֲלָפִים תִּשְׁעָה וְעֶשְׂרִֽים (Ezra 1:9), twenty nine knives, because they cut; and אֶת־שֶׁבַע מַחְלְפוֹת רֹאשִׁי (Shoftim 16:13), the seven locks of my head, are the curls of the hair, called so because they are like knives, or because change and exchange come over them when they whiten in old age.

שׁפח.sense: The שִׁפְחָה, a maidservant, with no masculine formed from it; and in a second sense the מִשְׁפָּחָה, a family, and so a tribe, and so a whole nation.

more.t: כְּעֵינֵי שִׁפְחָה אֶל־יַד גְּבִרְתָּהּ (Tehillim 123:2), as the eyes of a maid to the hand of her mistress; עֲבָדִים וּשְׁפָחוֹת (Koheles 2:7), menservants and maidservants; אֵין לְשִׁפְחָֽתְךָ כֹל (Melachim II 4:2), your maidservant has nothing. No masculine noun is formed from it: for the male one says עֶבֶד, a servant, and for the female אָמָה or שפחה, a maid.

מִשְׁפָּחָה וּמִשְׁפָּחָה (Esther 9:28), every single family, and לְמִשְׁפְּחֹתֵיהֶם יָֽצְאוּ מִן־הַתֵּבָֽה (Bereishis 8:19), they went out of the ark by their families. A tribe is called by it too: וַיַּקְרֵב אֶת־ מִשְׁפַּחַת יְהוּדָה (Yehoshua 7:17), he brought near the family of Yehudah, the tribe that is taken drawing near by families (Yehoshua 7:14).

וְאִם־ מִשְׁפַּחַת מִצְרַיִם (Zecharyah 14:18), and if the family of Mitzrayim; עַל כָּל־ הַמִּשְׁפָּחָה אֲשֶׁר הֶעֱלֵיתִי מֵאֶרֶץ מִצְרַיִם (Amos 3:1), against the whole family I brought up from the land of Mitzrayim; מִכֹּל מִשְׁפְּחוֹת הָֽאֲדָמָה (Amos 3:2), of all the families of the earth. And by a borrowing, וּפָֽקַדְתִּי עֲלֵיהֶם אַרְבַּע מִשְׁפָּחוֹת (Yirmiyahu 15:3), I will appoint over them four kinds.

שֹפח.sense: He gives no sense here. The entry is one pasuk of Yeshayahu, with a note that the word is treated at the letter samech.

more.t: The one pasuk is Yeshayahu 3:17, on קָדְקֹד בְּנוֹת צִיּוֹן, the crown of the daughters of Tzion. Of the word itself he says nothing here, only that he has already treated it at the letter samech.

אמה.sense: A maidservant, which he says is the same as a maid; but in one pasuk some read אַמָּתָהּ with a dagesh, and it is her arm.

more.t: וְגַם אֶת־בֶּן־ הָֽאָמָה (Bereishis 21:10), and also the son of the maidservant: the heh at the end is the feminine ending, and the root's own last heh drops, showing again in וְאַמְהֹתָיו וַיֵּלֵֽדוּ (Bereishis 20:17), and his maidservants, and they bore. Their sense is known, that they are maids.

וַתִּשְׁלַח אֶת־ אֲמָתָהּ (Shemos 2:5), she sent her maidservant. The reading is disputed: some read אַמָּתָהּ with a dagesh, from אַמָּה אָרְכּוֹ (Shemos 30:2), a cubit its length, and so Rav Saadiah Gaon explained it in his Arabic commentary, that she stretched out her arm.
